message:
The Windows-ARM64 Vulkan port: engine, overlay and the app tree as one coherent fork

This squashes the port's history into one commit on top of upstream baf16363 so the fork reads as a
single change: what it is, where it lives, and what has to pass.

The engine
  port/engine is strata-vk: a Vulkan-first front end (CLI, session/serve, per-model tuning, expert
  placement, NPU discovery, warmups).  It reports first-step, steady-state and prompt cost separately
  because averaging a cold first token into the rate hid a multi-second stall for several rounds.

The vendored tree and the overlay
  third_party/llama.cpp is vanilla ggml-org/llama.cpp at the pinned commit with
  port/llama-overlay-vanilla copied over it; it is fetched by port/tools/fetch-llama.ps1 and is not
  committed.  The overlay (60 files) carries the trellis/ternary types (TQK6/TQK7/TQ2_T/PTQ1_0) with
  their codecs, CPU kernels and Vulkan shaders, the MTB/NextN graft, the engine hooks, the qwen4exp
  features (hyper-connections, gated delta net, sparse indexer, per-layer embeddings), ggml_gated_mul,
  the ARM64 device tuning, and the fixes the packs on this machine needed.

Measured on this machine (Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme, Adreno X2-90)
  Gyro-S 9.7 tok/s decode / 212 prefill, Gyro-M 8.7 / 101, Q2_0 14.0 / 41.5, 27B Q4_0 7.8 / 162,
  35B-A3B 43.1 / 613.  Token streams are identical to the CPU backend on every pack.

Gates
  overlay reproduction byte-for-byte, 19 fork markers, the 10-check stdout contract, encoding and
  document audits, MUL_MAT/MUL_MAT_ID oracles for the trellis types, and the reference 32-token stream.

Documentation
  port/docs/README.md (quickstart), MAINTAINER.md (pin, overlay, sync, gates), ADRENO.md (the device
  and its measurements), UPSTREAM-PATCHES.md (per-patch provenance), features/ (hyper-connections, GDN,
  expert placement, NPU) and OPTIMIZATION-BACKLOG.md (everything measured and ruled out).

feat(engine): --parallel-recycle: adaptive batch slots with a backoff idle window

A one-GPU --serve start with several parallel (batch) slots reserves every slot's session and
verifier VRAM at load time.  On a 22 GB card at 256K that leaves the expert cache at roughly half
its one-slot size even when the server is idle and one request is running.

--parallel-recycle makes the slot reserve follow the load (--batch N becomes a cap):

  - the engine starts with no batch slot session, so the whole VRAM budget goes to the expert cache
    (measured at 256K: 6414 expert slots instead of ~3164 with 8 slots reserved);
  - a BGEN for an unreserved slot grows the layout first: one resize covers the whole queued burst
    and the BCO co-reads waiting for it, a failed resize rolls back, and a rollback that cannot
    rebuild the layout stops the engine instead of running with a mismatched layout;
  - once the burst is over the engine waits the min grace with no request in flight or queued, then
    frees every session (a solo request needs none, so the VRAM returns to the expert cache);
  - the grace starts at STRATA_PARALLEL_RECYCLE_MIN (default 2 s, plain integer seconds) and the
    upper bound is STRATA_PARALLEL_RECYCLE_MAX (default 600 s).  A batch request that follows a
    recycle within the maximum doubles the grace, once per recycle cycle, up to the maximum, so a
    burst every few seconds does not keep paying a shrink+grow pair; 3*max without any batch
    activity resets the grace to the minimum.  Setting the minimum equal to the maximum gives the
    fixed-window behaviour;
  - slots that stay reserved keep their sampling, penalties and logit_bias; with no slot reserved
    the solo path keeps its single-request defaults (tail-skip, PcieAuto);
  - a start whose canary cannot carve two slot sessions falls back to a normal start.

The option implies the segmented expert cache it needs (--vram-elastic, 512 MiB segments;
--vram-segment-mib overrides), so a start needs no second flag.

The idle shrink requires progress().busy == false, an empty input queue, no partial prompt pinned in a
slot and no waiting co-read request, and drops a BCO whose BGEN never came after 30 s by wall age; the co_set of the previous
request is not part of the guard (it is consumed by its BGEN), so STRATA_COALESCE_PREFILL does not
pin the layout.

Measured on an RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 256K with MTP (18K-token prompt, 480-token
output, parallel 4, max 300):
  - continuous single requests with 5 s gaps: 52.3 tok/s median (fixed 30 s window after a burst:
    47.5; one-slot start: 52.4);
  - four-way bursts every 10 s: the grace backs off 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16 s and the layout stops being
    recycled when the grace covers the burst period, which removes the per-burst shrink+grow pair;
  - 14 bursts at a 10 s period: no reset while the bursts continue; a 100 s quiet stretch then
    resets the grace once.

Tests: src/program/recycle_policy_test.cpp (base grace, one doubling per cycle, the max window and
cap, large-max saturation, activity-based reset, custom minimum, fixed mode, the integer parser) and
the existing adaptive_slots_test / slot_settings_test.  help, INFO (parallel_recycle=1
recycle_max= recycle_min= recycle_grace=) and docs/BATCHING.md describe the options.

prefill: STRATA_GDN_TC=2 runs the tensor-core GDN scan on sm_75 (Turing)

The chunked DeltaNet recurrence on the tensor cores needs sm_80 (m16n8k16, cp.async, redux.sync) and
98-125 KB of shared memory a block, so Turing cards stay on gdn_rec_cols_pipe_kernel. On sm_75:
- mma m16n8k16 f16 -> two m16n8k8 steps (k 0..7: a0 a1 b0, k 8..15: a2 a3 b1); ldmatrix is sm_75's;
- cp.async -> the existing plain-copy fallback; redux.sync -> the existing shuffle max;
- ONE plan (gdn_tc_scan_kernel<false, true, 3, 1, true>): every buffer single, 62,480 B (64 KB opt-in),
  the whole next chunk staged after the state update. gdn_rec_tc takes it on cc 7.5; the split variants
  stay unsupported there.
Opt-in: STRATA_GDN_TC=2. The server's 0.2.9 default (=1) leaves sm_75 on the old kernels, so the default
path does not change; sm_80+ cards run the same code as before.

[Engine] prompt read: STOP is seen by every stage of a layer split and between layers

A Stop during a long prompt read took effect only when the first card started its next 8192-token chunk, and the
second card read every chunk it was handed to the end: on 2x P100 the next request waited 18-20 s. Now every stage
checks STOP before each chunk (STRATA_STOP_STAGES=0: as before), and every stage checks between layers inside a
chunk (STRATA_STOP_LAYERS=0: as before), stops its expert copies, waits for its queued work and returns "cancelled".
Measured on 2x P100: the next request 17.9 -> 1.1 s and 20.1 -> 1.2 s; normal prompt reads unchanged; requests after
a stop in the middle of a chunk give the same logprobs as after the old stop.

[Engine] read tools from Anthropic tool_addition blocks (#5952)

Claude Code sends some tools as tool_addition blocks in a system message
inside `messages` instead of in the top-level `tools`. The block was an
unread type, so it was left out of the prompt, and anthropic_tools() did
not list the tool, so the model never saw it and a call for it would not
be read as a tool call.

The added tool's definition is now rendered where the client added it,
in the form a tool_reference loads a deferred tool, so the prompt's tool
list (and its cache) stays the same. anthropic_tools() includes it, so a
call is parsed against its schema. A tool already in the tool list, a
repeated addition, and a block without a definition add nothing.

feat(prefill): help the first and last chunks of multi-chunk split prompts

STRATA_PREFILL_HELP_FIRST=1 and STRATA_PREFILL_HELP_LAST=1 (opt-in, with
STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1) extend the layer split's prompt help to prompts read
in several chunks: the next stage helps the first stage's first chunk while
it still idles, and the first stage helps the last stage's final chunk once
it has handed everything on. The first-chunk help ends, its streams
settled, before the first hand-off, so the next stage reads its own chunks
with its own buffers.

fix(prefill): keep the P2P prompt help off when the cards cannot copy directly

When STRATA_PREFILL_HELP_P2P=1 finds no working peer path, the layer split's prompt help is now switched off instead of falling back to the mapped host route: that route's host buffers are what a RAM-short host cannot spare, and a share set for the direct path is not the host route's. The check also disables only the peer access it enabled itself, and its block now sits below split_help_env so that function keeps its comment. The setting is in the register, SETTINGS.md and MULTI_GPU.md (with a 2x RTX 2080 Ti NVLink measurement).
fix(serve): pass calls to undeclared tools through when the request declares ToolSearch

feat(prefill): opt-in peer copies for the layer split prompt help

STRATA_PREFILL_HELP_P2P=1 (with STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1) sends the helped chunk's activations to the helper card and takes its rows back with peer copies (NVLink or another direct path) instead of the mapped host route, so both PCIe links stay free for the streamed experts and the host buffers are not allocated. It is used only when both cards report peer access, enabling it succeeds and a test copy each way arrives exact; otherwise the engine logs why and keeps the host route.

RU: убран просроченный отпуск пути стенда из гейта -TextGate

Мерж апстрима 16.11 (tip main `74da7cf82`, уже запушен) оставил локальный гейт
текстов комплекта красным: список отпусков в `pack_kit.ps1` продолжал требовать
находку в файле, где её больше нет. Гейт вызывается из обоих workflow, поэтому
красным стал и `main`.

Что изменено?
- packaging/kit/ci/pack_kit.ps1 (+0/-2): из `$WEB_STAND_WAIVERS` удалён ключ
  `kit\strata_control\app_policy.py` (`hits = 1`, «литерал-заглушка реестра
  политик `_MODELS` (exe `C:/x/strata-dsv41.exe`)»). Отпуск описывал строку,
  которую коммит `efa9d6dbe` (11.11, «DeepSeek out (5/7)») вынес из
  `strata_control/app_policy.py`: в дельте мерж-базы `backup/engine-main-2026-11-16`
  против HEAD этот файл +8/-3, а `git grep -n 'C:/x/'` по `strata_control`,
  `strata_cli` и `serve` в HEAD не находит ничего. Алгоритм меры не менялся:
  `Split-StandPathHits` считает отпуск просроченным, когда ключ не сработал ни
  разу, и красит прогон ровно за это.

Зачем?
Просроченный отпуск - не косметика: он держит в списке то, что уже пора мерять
напрямую, и следующим шагом кто-то вернёт литерал «чтобы гейт позеленел». Смысл
списка - поимённо отпускать строки-подсказки пользователю и запасные значения
переменных окружения, а не молчать о файле, где находки больше не возможны.
Мерка специально различает три случая (лишняя находка, пропавшая находка,
несработавший ни разу отпуск), и этот прогон поймал именно третий.

Замеры?

The engine allocates the repacked gate/up matrices and a copy of the down matrices with cudaHostAlloc (about 16 GiB), so the kernel can neither swap them out nor evict them, and ends with 'cannot start' when the memory is not there. serve: a marker the reply quotes stays text, and a turn that ends mid-structure is continued

A control token's text cannot be generated: the literal re-tokenizes to the token that stops the
turn, so a reply quoting `<|im_end|>` was cut at the quote and ended as "stop" with nothing after it
(#537's shape, for the turn-end token).  The stop branch now reads the shape the token arrives in -
one backtick left over on its line, a ``` block open in the answer or in the thinking, or the
thinking with no code open - and in each of those the marker's text is written back as ordinary text
(#931's `plain` mechanism) and the turn goes on from there, bounded by QUOTED_MARKER_MAX and, for a
reply that only repeats the marker with no newline in between, by QUOTED_MARKER_RUN_MAX.  A turn-end
inside an unclosed block or inside the thinking is not an end either: the answer is continued instead
of stopping mid-structure.  Shape 3's exception is #728's loop - thinking that repeats whole passages
is a loop running on until the model writes its own end, not a marker the thought mentions, so
reasoning_repeat_coverage decides and the turn ends where the model ended it (which is what
serve/test_reasoning_loop_recovery.py expects: one pass with the recovery off).

OutputParser tracks the backtick run of the text that goes out - the content and the reasoning
region, tool arguments out, a run counted when it ends so one split across deltas counts once, a span
not reaching across its line - so the serve can tell a quoted marker from an ordinary turn-end:
`tick_run` (the run under the cursor), `quoted_marker` (that backtick is the one left over on its
line) and `unclosed_code`.  That is a second read of the same text next to #1058's `_track`
(`fence`/`line`/`ticks`), which answers where the NEXT character would sit - a paragraph's backtick
count, a fence opened at a line start - and cannot say what the character under the cursor is.  A
stop token with calls waiting in `pending` is #1058's settling point for a call written inside the
thinking, so it ends the turn rather than being read as a quote.  The stop ids get one source, the
tokenizer's control tokens, so the engine's --eos-ids, the serve's stopping and the write-back agree
(stop_texts, END_OF_TEXT); the thinking's text is kept as a capped tail (LOOP_TEXT_MAX) because both
the #728 look and the stop branch read it.

serve: STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE, park the prefix that fits

Parking refuses whole: when the outgoing chain does not fit the cache
byte budget or the physical-RAM floor, the entire snapshot is dropped
and the next request of that conversation re-reads from the root (or
token 0) - measured 225 s for a 160k-token chain.  The chain itself is
a depth ruler: walk it deepest-first and park the first checkpoint
prefix that passes both gates instead.  The parked copy keeps root +
chain + K/V [0, L), and mounts live on that checkpoint's running state
(the session state is deeper than L).  The next request mounts the
prefix and re-reads only the tail - the reply plus the new turn, which
the client re-renders anyway.  Single-stage only (the layer-split path
has no per-checkpoint byte split to walk); the below-min-tokens gate
already passed for the full chain and a truncated copy is parked even
under it - a root-deep mirror still saves the shared prefix.  The same
rule works the other way: an already-parked entry asked to make room
is shrunk to one of its own checkpoints (K/V pages past the landing,
the deeper checkpoints' running states and their ids go, the landing's
state moves into live) before it is dropped whole; a landing below
--conversation-cache-min-tokens is not worth a slot and the entry goes
whole.  Truncation obeys the borrowed-donor guard the same way eviction does:
shrinking a donor mid-restore would put the borrowed prefix outside
the donor (the restore ERR).  Off unless STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE=1; the
environment variable is the only switch (no flag).

cache: hand the parked copy's spread checkpoints back to a slot-mounted chain

A batch slot keeps at most one checkpoint of the conversation it serves, so
every main-chain switch that returns through a slot (slot_source mount)
rebuilds the checkpoint pool from that single point. The checkpoints the read
spread along the chain survive only on the parked copy, and the truncate-park
ladder (STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE) starves of shallow rungs: measured overnight, a
205k chain parked under RAM pressure skipped whole ("skip parking (physical
RAM admission; need 5949 MiB ...)") because its only remaining checkpoints sat
at >=196k and every shallower rung had been lost to a switch.

merge_pool() finds the most recently parked copy of the same conversation
(cvec match, prefix-compatible checkpoints) and copies back every
prefix-compatible point the chain does not already hold. The used stamps
travel, so returned survivors age from their last hit and the normal
retention policy thins them again. Text only for now: an empty image list
never matches a checkpoint that carries image keys. STRATA_POOL_RESTORE=0
turns the return off (default on).

The documentation had no reference for most of the engine's settings. The flag list
existed only in --help, the environment variables only in the source, and the server
options only in argparse. This change adds one page per surface, a documentation index,
and a style guide.

  area, plus the three ways to set a flag.
- docs/ENVIRONMENT.md: all 617 runtime environment variables with default and effect, the
  61 compile-time macros kept separate, and the precedence rule.
- docs/SERVER.md: the 30 server options, the run config keys, all 34 routed paths, the
  per-request tune keys and the process lifetime.
- docs/TERMINAL.md: every strata command and subcommand, the profile/runtime model, and
  the exit codes.

The harness's record joined to the engine's, turn by turn (tools/agent_profile.py, section 8), showed that with 16
agents on 8 sessions 39.5% of all the time spent reading prompts went to cells the thread had held: threads under
4,096 cells were not parked, and a parked thread came back at its prompt's end and read its whole last answer again.

  earlier checkpoint.
- STRATA_Q36_PARK_MIN: 4,096 -> 256 cells.

  two part; later threads copy those cells and restore that state.

- agent_bench: a harness line over 20,000 characters keeps its structure (its long strings are cut), it was cut
  mid-record before.

16 real agents on 8 sessions, before -> now: prompt tokens read 309,650 -> 202,070; cells a thread held and read
again 119,407 -> 28,501; reading prompts 24.5% -> 17.3% of the run; an agent's first prompt 670 -> 148 ms; parking a
cache 163 -> 223 ms; 170.4 -> 177.8 tok/s over the run.

[Engine] SYCL/xe: refuse a HOST-mode start whose mirror does not cover the expert set

The request report counts cache hits and PCIe reads and never host-computed experts: there is no host
expert path on this port. So an expert that is in neither VRAM nor the mirror is served by nothing, and a
window that routes to one stays finite and is wrong - measured as '!!!!' on UD-IQ1_M with a 16 GiB
mirror, against '391' on the same pack with a 31 GiB one.

The NO_HOST=1 path already refuses this state. This does the same when the host is expected to answer:
if fewer experts were mirrored than were missing from VRAM, say how many and how to fix it, and stop -
rather than answering wrongly.

Measured after the change, UD-IQ1_M with the mirror left to auto: 20030 of 23282 mirrored, and
"REFUSED: 3252 of 23282 experts are neither in VRAM nor mirrored" instead of garbage. The set needs
about 42 GiB of mirror (23282 x 1.97 MB), which is what the message tells the user to provide.

[Other] The engine's own chat: the Strata tools know which server they belong to

On chudmax (0.2.14-mbp.rtx.1, Q2_0, an API key set) the model in the web chat
called the built-in Strata tools and concluded that the running server was "not
what's serving me". Three things led it there:

- strata_status called its own server "started outside this MCP server";
- the tools looked for models in the Terminal's code folder, where an installed
  Terminal keeps none ("no model is installed in .../terminal/0.1.60");
- the tools had no API key for the server that started them (HTTP 401 on the
  speed test, and no engine version or timings in the status).

The serving process now tells its tools who it is (serve/mcp.py: the config,
port and key go to the child as STRATA_MCP_HOST_CONFIG, _PORT and _KEY, and the
tools' folder is the one the config is in). tools/strata_mcp.py then:

- marks that server "this_chat" in strata_status and says so in the summary
  and in the MCP instructions;
- uses its key for its own requests (never in an answer);
- reads its config and, by default, its engine log;
- refuses to stop it from inside its own chat, with force or without;
- answers a speed test from inside the chat's own turn with the timings of the
  last finished request, since no second request can be timed then.

Without the variables nothing changes: an assistant that starts the tools
itself gets the old behaviour.

[Pack] keep a Q8_0 hyper-connection projection in the GGUF

The engine's STRATA_HC_Q8 read takes these projections from the GGUF's own Q8_0 bytes, so converting them
into dense.bin is waste: it was 1.18 GiB of a 1.5 GB dense.bin and most of the arena that is sized from it.

    before: dense.bin 1538 MB, 195 tensors converted
    after:  dense.bin  267 MB,   1 tensor converted (ple_conv1d, which the kernel requires as F16)

A Q8_0 source stays in the GGUF; anything else - the F32 inject rows included - keeps the FORM path, so a
model whose projections are not Q8_0 is unaffected.  The iq_pack tests carry the new contract.

[Engine] SYCL: load a pack's shape-only projection row (STRATA_HC_Q8)

With iq_pack leaving those tensors in the GGUF, the pack's index carries a shape-only row for them (code_bits
set, dst_bytes 0) and WeightTable::load refused the whole pack: "this pack holds the tensor only in its GGUF
form".  Under STRATA_HC_Q8 such a row becomes a normal table entry with no arena storage - the type and shape
are all the read needs, and native_dense uploads the Q8_0 copy it consumes.  Without the env the error is
unchanged, so a pack that expects a BF16 copy still gets one.

[Engine] SYCL: read the hyper-connection projections from Q8_0 bytes

Port of the CUDA engine's read (src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu, the one STRATA_HC_Q8=1 selects): the
hyper-connection projections are taken from the pack's Q8_0 bytes instead of from BF16 copies dequantized at
pack time, which is 1.18 GiB of VRAM on a card where the expert cache wants it.

  - sycl/include/strata/kernels/q8_block.hpp: the Q8_0 block format (34 B: fp16 d + 32 int8), scale(), value(),
    four() and row_bytes() - no policy, so it can be checked on its own;
  - gr_down_q8_kernel / gr_up_q8_kernel: the two passes, with the same grid, lane map and per-(token, chunk,
    row) partials as the CUDA kernels, so the plan and the reduce see the layout they already expect.  The
    Q8_0 codes are read as two 16-bit halves, as CUDA does;
  - fused_gr_read_multi takes the Q8 pair when the caller provides one, and returns false because it writes no
    q8_1 image of the mixed residual (STRATA_QFUSE is separate) - the caller then quantizes as for any other
    read;
  - the read's partials come from fused_gr_set_q8_scratch: Verifier::init allocates them outside any capture
    (a USM allocation inside a captured window aborts the engine) and outside the bump allocator, whose layout
    the windows are sized against.

The read writes only what the BF16 multi read writes - mixed, rs, inject_out and R_out - and nothing else: an
early version also stored the low-rank vector into a.lo, which is the engine's lo_ workspace shared with the
PLE block, and that corrupted the model while every kernel parity stayed green.

[Engine] SYCL/Q8: the Q8_0 read's parity suite

Five card-level tests, each comparing the kernel against a CPU reference or against the engine's own BF16 read:

  - q8_block_test (host, no card): the block decode, two blocks with positive and negative scales;
  - q8_down_parity: the down pass, every (token, row) partial against a double dot product over the same
    dequantized weights - worst 1.0e-05 of the L1 norm at the window's real token count (6);
  - q8_up_parity: three checks, because one cannot tell a wrong block offset from fp32 summation order -
    zero partials (the gate is exactly 0.5), one non-zero weight per row at block and step boundaries, then
    dense weights;
  - q8_apply_parity: the inputs the engine uses and the plain fixture did not - apply=true (the residual gate)
    and a non-null w_inject - where R_out and inject_out must agree exactly and do (0 and 7e-07); mixed is
    reported, not asserted, because it is a difference of four nearly equal stream terms and a cross-weight
    comparison moves it on the columns that cancel;
  - q8_read_parity: the whole read against a double-precision reference of the formula, each path over its own
    weights (q8 1e-05, bf16 2e-05).

The inject case earns its own test: the block computes its rows only when q8_inject or w_inject is set, and a
regression there made the read sum zeros for inject_out while everything else looked correct.

27B conversation cache: sized by the machine, threads told apart for any client

The memory tier for parked threads no longer needs a budget. Without
--conversation-cache-mib it follows the machine: a cache is parked while
that leaves --conversation-cache-min-free-mib of host memory available
(not given: a fifth of the machine's memory), and when other programs take
memory the oldest parked caches leave it again (looked at before a park, at
every request, every two seconds while idle). A number fixes a budget, 0
turns the tier off.

Which thread a request is no longer assumes a system turn and a user
message: a session remembers where the last turn of its thread's first
prompt began (Sess::thread_head), and a request that shares more than that
prompt is the same thread. Holds with or without a system prompt or tools.

  the longest start of its prompt: with a shared tool list, another
  thread's session. Now another thread's prefix is copied into an empty
  session, else the one used longest ago (STRATA_Q36_SOLO_KEEP).

  decoding (STRATA_Q36_ADM_CKPT_BUSY). Only the prefix is copied now.

  now parked in host memory (--conversation-cache-mib) and, when that is
  full, in the spill folder (--conversation-cache-spill-dir), with the
  thread's prefix checkpoint; it comes back into whatever session the
  thread's next request gets. Off unless a budget or a folder is given.

27B batch server: the slot of a lone request's session holds its chat

27B batch server: the slot of a lone request's session holds its chat

A request that runs alone on a --batch engine runs in a session the engine
chooses. The server did not know which one: it still counted that session's
slot as empty, sent the next request into it, and that request's read
replaced the first one's chat while an empty slot stood by. The chat's next
turn then read its whole history again.

The engine now ends such a request's DONE line with session=<slot>
held=<tokens>, and the server counts that slot as holding the chat.

Four agents, 26K-token conversations, a second turn the held state does not
continue: 13.5 s (one of four re-read 26,130 tokens) -> 2.4 s (all four kept
26,086). The four answers equal those of a full re-read.

[Engine] two opt-in decode experiments from Basalt: the cumulative draft rule and a next-layer L2 prefetch

Both are off by default; the default path is unchanged.

- STRATA_DRAFT_CUM=<threshold> (include/strata/core/draft_cum.hpp, ported from Basalt, MIT): the MTP chain keeps
  drafting while the product of the drafts' binned acceptance rates stays at or above a per-request threshold
  (STRATA_DRAFT_CUM_ADAPT=0 keeps it fixed). The chain rule and the serve window rule compute the same float
  products. Serial serve on one stage only.
- STRATA_L2_NEXT=1: while a layer waits for the CPU tier's rows, a bulk L2 prefetch (cp.async.bulk.prefetch, sm_90+)
  reads the next layer's non-expert device weights; STRATA_L2_NEXT_MIB caps the bytes per layer.

[Engine] NVIDIA sm_75: a defaults table, so a Turing card runs the measured kernels

The sm_75 series ships off unless STRATA_SM75_PERF=1, because nobody on the team had an
sm_75 card to confirm it, and nv_defaults had a table for sm_86, sm_60 and sm_121 but not
for 7.5.  This adds the missing one, in the same shape as the others: the off switch is
STRATA_SM75_PERF=0, a variable the user set wins, and every other architecture's table is
unchanged.

Measured on an RTX 2080 Ti (sm_75, driver 610.57.04, nvcc 13.0 -arch=sm_75) against the
kernels they replace, the series turns on:

  STRATA_PA_V1_PREFETCH  prompt attention (int8 KV)  1.72x, bit-identical
  STRATA_ATTN_V3         decode attention            1.40-2.12x (2.0-2.1x at 2-8 queries), bit-identical
  STRATA_TOPK_SPLIT      decode top-k                1.06-11.54x, same ids (grows with --max-context)
  STRATA_SCORES_THREAD   prompt scorer               2.95-8.23x, bit-identical

The first is the one that makes the others matter: the shared K/V buffer takes a block's
shared memory from 37.9 to 29.2 KB, and that is the difference between one block per SM
and two on a 64 KB Turing SM.  The kernel is latency-bound, not tensor-core-bound:
removing half of every MMA saves 11%, and replacing the int8->half2 conversion with a
passthrough saves nothing.

The table also sets STRATA_PA_V2T: Turing then takes the v2 prompt-attention kernel
(register staging instead of cp.async) instead of v1, 1.24-1.33x.  That one sums in another
order - 2.1e-07 relative RMS from v1 - so the table is deliberately not described as
"exact" in the line the engine prints, unlike the sm_86 and sm_60 tables.

It is a defaults table rather than a change to each gate on purpose: is_sm75() alone would
have made those kernels unreachable for the documented STRATA_SM75_PERF=0, and this keeps
one switch that turns the whole card's tuning off.

[Docs] Deferring the refill is refuted: decode 92 → 0.4 tok/s for 72–188 ms of TTFT

perf: deferring the refill is refuted - decode falls from 92 to 0.4 tok/s

I built the flag (STRATA_REFILL_DEFER, one if in the serve prompt path,
default unchanged) precisely because the refill looked like dead weight:
it costs 0.319 ms per lent slot and runs between the read and "prompt
done", so the first token waits 72-188 ms for it.

Measured on the same ladder, six samples per size:

  tokens   refill kept   refill deferred   decode kept   decode deferred
  126        398 ms        2,945 ms          92.0 tok/s      30.9
  456        539 ms        3,126 ms          91.8           0.5
  1608      1,468 ms        3,953 ms          74.3           0.4

The per-sample sequence says why: at 126 tokens requests 1-2 are normal
(0.553, 0.537 s) and request 3 is 3.069 s - the collapse starts once the
cache holds the previous prompt's experts. The borrowed slots ARE the
decode working set, so the refill is a prefetch for the tokens about to be
generated. Skipping it moves the cost from one transfer per request to a
streamed fetch per token.

So item 1 of the ranked list closes as refuted, with the numbers, and item
2 becomes the narrower and surviving question: not when to refill but how
much - only the experts the first decode positions route are worth
pre-loading.

A/B driver, the analysis script.

home is sycl/, so it compiles sycl/src/program/generate.cpp - patching

  `hashFiles` is only evaluated after checkout and is unusable in workflow-level env; the step text

A late failure no longer wipes the cache: the next run starts from ready objects and compiles only

EN: Release CI: build directories of both engines are cached between runs

Compilation is the longest step of the release run, and it always started from an empty
directory: only the CUDA redist archives were cached, not the objects. The local full build
of 14 Nov (kit502/kit503) measured what remains with ready objects - that share is what we cut.

What changed?
- `.github/workflows/kit-release.yml` (+19/-0): an `actions/cache@v4` step before the engine
  build, paths `strata\build-kit` and `llama\build-kit`. The key carries `runner.os`,
  `CUDA_VERSION`, `ARCH` and `hashFiles` of every `CMakeLists.txt` of both engines and the
  ggml pin: a configuration change gives an exact miss and a full rebuild, while
  `restore-keys` pulls the previous directory and cmake rebuilds what changed by mtime.
  A toolchain or architecture change alters ABI and cubin, so such directories are not
  shared across keys. No extra guard was needed: `Assert-FreshCache` in `build_kit.ps1`
  already checks `CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` and refuses to build inside a foreign cache.

Why?
Previously every `kit-release.yml` run paid a full compilation of both engines for three
architectures, although only a handful of files change between releases. Now a repeated run
compiles only the changed units, while a run after a CMake change stays full, as it should.

Verified
- Locally `build_kit.ps1 -Engines "strata;llama" -Arch 86;89;120 -SkipProbe` with ready
  objects: strata - configure 4.6 s, build 772.4 s (21 compiles, 3 links, 174 objects
  before the run); llama - configure 2.2 s, build 6 s (1 compile, 4 links, 315 objects
  before the run). Both runs are marked "partial build" - that is exactly the share the
  cache removes.
- Architectures proven by cubin/PTX: `strata-q36`, `strata`, `ggml-cuda` - sm_86, sm_89,
  sm_120 (`ggml-cuda` carries 120 in the 120a form).
- The YAML parses with `yaml.safe_load`: 18 steps, the new step in place, no parse errors.
- A cold full build in CI did not run in this pass - the cache effect will be checked by
  the duration of the "Сборка обоих движков" step in the first live run.

Accepted remainder?
The first run after this commit still has an empty cache, so it stays full-length; the gain
shows from the second run. ccache was not installed: the build-directory cache gives the same
effect without adding a toolchain.

Result
A repeated release run rebuilds only changed units instead of both engines entirely; cache
correctness is held by the CMakeLists key and the existing home-directory check.

Prompts in three stages: --prompt-split L,M gives the tier after the first a middle stage (its GPU runs each chunk's layers L..M-1, the experts its cache lacks on the second GPU), off by default

Before, a long prompt ran in at most two stages, the main GPU's and the second GPU's, and a third GPU took no part in
prompts.

- prefill/split: PromptSplit holds one or two later stages (Stage: its first layer, its device, its tier's cache and
  residency, its runner on the second GPU), each a Prefill of its own on its GPU with a thread of its own, its weights
  and state copies in a region its cache lends (Region); it is no SplitOut itself: each later stage is one (Impl::St),
  fed by the stage before it through pinned memory.  A middle stage hands its residual on (Prefill::out_done: a chunk's
  rows go in once the last one's have gone out) and tells the next stage whether a chunk ends the first stage's run
  (Prefill::set_run_end).  A stage without a runner copies ahead as over an x16 link and keeps its GPU's queue short
  (the last one, on the second GPU, which runs the others' shares too); every stage needs an attention layer; the last
  runs the draft layer's K/V.  A stage's worker turns an exception into the stage's error.
- prefill/experts: a remote runner's calls restore the caller's GPU (OnDevice), not the main one: a middle stage's
  thread drives its runner on the second GPU.
- core/session: ckpt_parts forms a stage's parts for its layers [lo, hi) alone.  It read the states of every layer from
  the stage's first on, past the end of a middle stage's arrays: once in ~10 three-stage prompts the engine ended
  without a word.
- generate.cpp: --prompt-split L[,M]; with one tier, L,M runs two stages split at (L + M) / 2.  PromptBuffers: the
  middle stage's runner (offload_mid) and region, that tier's loan (loan3, refilled through its adaptive tier), a
  region per stage (split_regions); the image position table copied to every later stage's GPU; --second-gpu-clocks
  holds a middle stage's card from the prompt's first chunk; generate mode's lines and --prefill-profile for the third

serve: restore a session file without holding its K/V in RAM

The RESTORE path materialized the whole snapshot in host memory, so a deep
session could not be restored on a machine that serves it: upstream's own
documented 503 'when the RAM to read the file is not there'.  The restore is
now two passes over the same file, format v1 unchanged:

- the read pass parses and validates the whole file (running state, K/V
  headers, every count against this session's limits, the payload hash)
  without materializing the K/V; it reports each layer's part sizes.
- the apply pass re-reads the file and copies the K/V into the authoritative
  pools a 16 MiB block at a time.  It is bound to the read pass: a file whose
  layer count or any part size differs is refused before that part is applied,
  and the payload hash is compared to the trailer at the end.  The first
  applied block is the gate - before it a failure refuses cleanly, after it
  the engine fail-stops rather than decode from bytes it cannot vouch for.

Peak RAM is two 16 MiB buffers and the running-state metadata, so a session
of any depth restores under the same floor.  Measured on a 198,830-token
IQ3_S session: 3.05 GiB restored in 3.4-3.5 s, next turn 99.99% reused.
The residency refill after the pool writes is mandatory for the modes that
keep K/V in VRAM and runs per layer (kv_stream_reset / kv_ring_restore).

[Engine] dflash2: find the head's top 16 by a bound and a ranking, not 16 serial picks

topk_part / topk_merge picked the 16 best one at a time, each pick a block-wide reduction with two
barriers. The order (value desc, index asc) is total, so the top 16 is a fixed list that can be found
in parallel. Each value and its index become one 64-bit key that orders like better() (-0 as +0).
Each warp sorts its 32 threads' bests (bitonic); the 16th best of the block's 256 thread bests,
found by binary search over the 8 warps' 16 best, is a bound no better than the block's 16th best.
Only values at or above it can be in the top 16: at most 15 * PER + 1 of them (241 for a chunk,
61 for the merge), and each one's place is the count of those better than it. The values written are
the original floats, so the lists are bitwise the same.

nsys per kernel, RTX 5080 (sm_120, CUDA 13), 7 rows of 248,320 logits: part 23.3 -> 12.6 us,
merge 6.6 -> 3.0 us. dflash2_round_bench (400 rounds, median of 7) 1.4195 -> 1.4068 ms GPU a
round, digest unchanged. Default on (solo and batch); STRATA_DF2_TOPK_RANK=0 restores the serial picks.

dflash2_q4_parity checks ranked vs serial on 5 shapes (ties, -inf, short and empty chunks, a row with
no candidate, all of a chunk's best in one thread, +0/-0 ties with denormals): bitwise equal.
Mutations (one index off; -0 not folded) are reported as MISMATCH. HIP compiles the same file
(wave32; 64-bit shuffles through __shfl_xor); not built or run here.

[Engine] dflash2: score the selector's walk in one parallel launch, then walk the table

Every predecessor the candidate selector's walk can reach is the anchor (row 0) or one of row i-1's 16
candidates, so all the walk's step scores form a table T[row][prev candidate][candidate] that does not
depend on the walk's choices. select_table_kernel fills it with one block per (prev, row), using the
walk's own select_eval_step, so the scores are bitwise the same. The beam walk then runs over T in
shared memory: one warp per beam, back-pointers instead of path copies, two barriers per row. The
greedy walk (STRATA_DF2_BEAM=1) reads the same table.

EN: start.ps1: the failure path names the engine exit code as a number

In the live 5080 log (a foreign machine, launched from the unpacked archive) the kit
printed "Server exited with code ." and "[FAIL] server did not come up (code )". The
cause is not the engine but how ExitCode is read from a process started without -Wait.

What changed?
- packaging/kit/start.ps1 (+23/-2): added `Get-ProcExitCode` (:51) with a comment
  (:43-50) listing the five probe variants of 14.11 and their actual outcomes, because the
  earlier remedy ("touch `$proc.Handle`") was disproved by that same probe: the function
  returns `$null` while the process is alive or if `ExitCode` is empty, otherwise the
  number. Right after `Start-Process ... -PassThru`, `$proc.EnableRaisingEvents = $true`
  is set (:232): without it Windows PowerShell 5.1 silently leaves `ExitCode` empty, and
  setting it later is impossible - the exit moment is already missed. Both failure prints
  (:252, :257) emit `$shown` - a number or the word "unavailable" - instead of the empty
  `$($proc.ExitCode)` substitution.

Why?
A person at a foreign machine could not tell from the refusal text what killed the engine:
an empty "(code )" does not distinguish "engine returned 0 but never served", "code could
not be read" and "process is still alive". Now the failure either names the code or says
outright that it is unavailable.

Verified
Mechanics probe (E:/tmp/kit360_exitcode_probe_2026-11-14.ps1, taken 14.11, launch without
-Wait, engine replaced by `cmd /c exit 7`): `ExitCode` as-is - empty; touching
`$proc.Handle` - empty; `WaitForExit()` after `HasExited` - empty;
`EnableRaisingEvents=$true` immediately after start - 7; the same plus `WaitForExit()` - 7.
Acceptance (glm/scripts/kit360_exitcode_accept_2026-11-14.ps1, run 14.11, engine replaced
by `where.exe`): MAIN run - fixed source in the staging layout of the archive (bin\ next
to kit\), 4 checks green, text contains "Server exited with code 2" and "(code 2)";
CONTROL - the previous carrier dist/gpu-infer-kit/kit/start.ps1 on the same base, the same
checks red, text contains "code ." and "(code )". The measure does distinguish the fix.
The expected code is no longer hardcoded: it is taken independently by repeating in the
acceptance exactly the command the kit printed on its "Launch:" line, with
-Wait -PassThru. Hence base 2, not the earlier "1" taken from the trimmed
`where.exe --native dummy.gguf` call (the first version of the acceptance went red on the
fixed carrier).

Accepted remainder
"unavailable" stays a valid answer for a live process - honest, and it does not change log
triage. The Strata branch of the archive still receives a CLI command with no HTTP mode,
so the promised webui address would not have opened on the 5080 even with the fixed text -
that is a separate change, not this diff.

Result

Engine: one-token IQ2_XXS / IQ2_XS / IQ1_M rows on AVX2 CPUs without AVX-512, bit for bit equal to ggml-cpu's dot

One token of an IQ2_XXS or IQ2_XS expert row ran ggml-cpu's own AVX2 vec_dot on both lanes. One token of IQ1_M ran Strata's row_dot_iq1m<1>, which on this Broadwell is 1.5x slower than ggml-cpu's dot (42 vs 28 ns per block). iq_own1_rows (iq_avx2.cpp) computes the same sums in the same order as ggml-cpu (int32 lanes, f16(d) * y.d, one fmadd per block), but unpacks each block's indices, signs and scales with SIMD instead of a scalar table walk. It is ported from a llama.cpp fork's ggml_vec_dot_iq2_xxs_q8_K / _iq2_xs_ / _iq1_m_, with the one pext (microcoded on AMD Zen 1/2) replaced by shifts. It is wired into the Qwen lane's one-token rows (native_expert.cpp) and the DeepSeek lane's one-token dots (ds4_gg_cpu.cpp, behind own_ok).

Gate: the CPU and ggml-cpu both report AVX2 + FMA + F16C, and the CPU has no AVX-512 (neither the VBMI tier nor the 0.2.12 VNNI/BW tier). The rows were measured only on such a CPU; AVX-512 CPUs keep their paths. Each type is checked bit for bit against ggml-cpu's dot on the running CPU at first use, and falls back if any bit differs. STRATA_CPU_IQ_OWN1=0 turns it off. Other quant types (Q4_K / Q5_1 / Q8_0, the UD-Q4_K_XL pack) are not touched. The code is plain intrinsics with an MSVC __forceinline, so the file builds under /arch:AVX2 as before (not compiled with MSVC here).

Measured 2026-11-10 on 2x Xeon E5-2699 v4 (Broadwell, AVX2, 2 nodes), this commit on dbb2d168, iq_own1_bench --bench. Median of 3 runs, new rows vs the current default:

  1 thread, from cache, ns per block (n = 2560 / 7168 weights per row)
    IQ2_XXS  28.2 -> 22.2 / 27.5 -> 21.3   (0.77-0.79x the time)
    IQ2_XS   31.2 -> 21.2 / 30.9 -> 20.7   (0.67-0.68x)
    IQ1_M    29.5 -> 21.9 / 27.6 -> 20.8   (0.74-0.75x; against Strata's own row_dot_iq1m<1> about 0.5x)
  44 threads, from DRAM, GB/s, node-local (n = 2560 / 7168)
    IQ2_XXS  67.3 -> 68.8 / 40.6 -> 50.6   IQ2_XS 67.7 -> 69.1 / 56.5 -> 55.1   IQ1_M 60.3 -> 68.1 / 36.0 -> 44.1
  44 threads, memory on one node: 0.99-1.00x at n = 2560, 0.95-1.09x at n = 7168

On one thread the rows take a quarter to a third less time per block. With every core streaming from DRAM the CPU lane is bandwidth-bound and they are about equal: +2 % at n = 2560 for the IQ2 types, +13 % for IQ1_M. The n = 7168 node-local numbers are noisy (ranges in the run up to 20 %), and IQ2_XS there reads 2-5 % lower. The win is per core, so it shows where the CPU lane runs fewer threads than the memory can feed. Not measured end to end: no DeepSeek pack or Qwen IQ2 pack was on the box.

  max_rows rounded up to the tile width. A launch has a fixup only where its tiles (experts x tiles across max_rows

[Docs] The block says how far the harvest has got: block_harvest

A miss and a not-yet-filed fact looked identical to the reader. The header told
how much of the store is in view (`shown="3 of 2,106 active"`) and nothing about
freshness, while the turn queue on this box runs a median 6.92 h from said to
written and drains only on 240 s of engine silence - 1 pending at midnight, 1,300
on a heavy day. The question came from `fieldnotes_ai` on Moltbook, 2026-11-13.

- `memory.block_harvest` (default false, so the tracked path stays byte-identical)
  adds one attribute to the header: harvest="current|fresh|lagging|backlog" from
  the pending-turn count, buckets 0 / <=5 / <=50 / more. Five is the sweep's own
  tick threshold, so `fresh` means "the next tick will catch it".
- QUANTIZED because the block is pinned per conversation by an LRU with no TTL:
  an exact count would churn the pin on every filing and spend the prefill the
  cache exists to save. Four words = at most three byte changes per queue crossing,
  and the word describes the BLOCK, the same contract as the facts under it and the
  pin-time `version=` it already carries.
- Counted in the same lock section as n_active (one extra query, served by the
  partial index turns_pending).
- serve/test_memory.py BlockHarvestTest, 4 cases: off is today's bytes, the four
  buckets, a pinned conversation replays byte-identically inside a bucket, and a
  draining queue moves backlog -> lagging -> current. Red on the bucket arithmetic
  first (I expected `lagging` from 90-85=5, which is `fresh`), green after.

Duo: do not load the other host's dense weights

Each host loaded the dense (non-expert) weights of all 40 layers, and
the prefix host also the output head it never uses. A host now loads
only its own layers' dense weights, and only the suffix host loads the
head. This gives about 2.9 GB per host back to the resident experts,
which is what decides the speed.

Duo: conversation slots for a pair

Strata's server sets a conversation aside when another one arrives and
takes it back later instead of reading its prompt again. For a pair the
state lives on two hosts, so slot_save on the suffix host now collects
its own half and the prefix host's half over the link into one blob,
and slot_load puts both halves back or neither. The server's RAM and
folder slots hold the blob whole and work unchanged; a prefix host that
restarts has lost nothing.

A pair's slot identity ends in the cut, and a pair's default slot
folder is <pack>/slots-duo, so one host's slots are never offered to a
pair or the other way round. The identity the hosts compare at connect
time now includes the number of restore points.

The one-host slot format is unchanged.

Duo: split DeepSeek V4.1 Flash by layers over two hosts

Add a two-host mode to the DeepSeek V4.1 Metal engine (strata_ds4).
One process, the prefix host (--duo-listen ADDR --duo-allow PEER), runs
layers [0, K) and the Engram rows; the other, the suffix host
(--duo-connect ADDR), runs layers [K, 40), the head and the sampler and
is the one a server talks to. --duo-cut K sets the cut; 20 is the cut
this model allows, because the hand-off has to sit at a KV source layer.

Both processes are the same engine with the same pack. The suffix host
repeats every call that changes the conversation's state (a window's
tokens, reset, checkpoint, mark, pin, restore) to the prefix host over
one TCP stream, and the prefix host answers each window with the
hand-off: the same rows (h | pre | topk | cand) the engine already moves
between two GPUs of one machine.
The two hosts compare an identity string at connect time (engine
version, model geometry, model files by base name and size, cut,
context) and refuse to pair when it differs. Each host prints its own
share of the time at exit.

Why: a 96 GB Mac cannot keep this model's experts in memory and reads
most of them from disk for every token. Two such Macs can each keep one
half resident.

This commit has the windowed path and a plain TCP link only. With every
routed expert on the CPU lane (--vram-experts 0.0) a split run on one
machine gives the same tokens as the unsplit engine.

Duo link: TLS 1.3 with mutual authentication

The link between the two hosts carries token ids and activations, so it
is now encrypted and authenticated by default. A build with
-DSTRATA_DUO_TLS=ON (static OpenSSL 3 from STRATA_DUO_OPENSSL_ROOT)
accepts --duo-certs DIR, a directory with ca.crt and this host's role
certificate and key:

  prefix host:  strata-stage-worker.crt / .key
  suffix host:  strata-stage-coordinator.crt / .key

Each side verifies the other's certificate against the private CA and
checks its role (the certificate's DNS subjectAltName), so a worker
admits only a coordinator and the other way round. TLS 1.3 only, ALPN
"strata-duo-1", no session tickets, no compression. The prefix host's
source-address check (--duo-allow) stays in front of the handshake, and
it sends a short tag after its own checks so that a refusal is reported
at connect time.

Without --duo-certs the link refuses to open unless --duo-insecure asks
for the plain stream. A default build (STRATA_DUO_TLS off) is unchanged
apart from refusing --duo-certs with a message that says how to build.

The transport design follows the stage-RPC transport of the Linux/CUDA
fork by petria (branch rpc-v0.2.13), which was used as the reference.

Duo: read long prompts in chunks across the two hosts

The first version read every prompt in windows of 16 tokens, each with
its own round trip, which is slow for long prompts. A long prompt now
goes through the engine's chunked path on both hosts: the suffix host
sends the run's tokens and layout once, the prefix host runs its layers
over each chunk and streams that chunk's hand-off rows back, and the
suffix host runs its layers and the head on them. Both hosts keep the
run's restore points from their own layers, so a later restore gives
the same state as after windows.

The chunk is 2048 rows by default (--prefill-chunk N on both hosts, or
DS4_DUO_CHUNK; 0 selects the windows of 16 again). The chunk size is
part of the identity the hosts compare.

A run of chunks across the hosts is not interrupted: a Stop takes
effect after the read.

With a fixed summation order (DS4_SUM_BY_EXPERT=1 DS4_SPEC_WASTE=1e9)
the chunked path of a split run on one machine gives the same tokens as
the unsplit engine; at default settings the order of the sums differs
by one unit in the last place.

fix(prefill): give the MoE MMQ row-id table a read-past-end margin

The prompt path carved the MMQ identity row map (`Product::ids`) to
exactly its row capacity. The ggml MMQ kernels copy a whole J-wide tile
of ids from each expert's first row, and the stream-k fixup reads a tile
past the last expert's rows, so a launch over a full batch reads past the
end of the map. It is the last buffer the arena's `carve()` hands out, so
the read runs off the end of the device allocation and faults.

Add `mmq::ids_table_rows(n) = n + roundup(n, 128) + 128`, at least the
furthest read any launch that map serves makes (its `total_rows` and
`max_rows` are both at most `n`), and size and fill the map with it.
`bytes_needed()` runs the same `carve()`, so the arena grows with it.
This is the same margin the repo's `mmq_tab_parity` already gives its row
map for the same tile read; production's carve did not.

Reproduced on an RTX 4090 (sm_89) under compute-sanitizer: an exactly-sized
map reports 3877 invalid reads and an illegal access, the padded map
reports 0. The extra entries are inert, the product is byte-identical with
the tail zeroed over five seeds. `mmq_ident_margin` gates both; its
memcheck case registers only when compute-sanitizer is on PATH.

EN: Marker gate holds the number-snapshot shape; the measure lives in the repo

What was impossible before: our commit counts (89 for Strata, 15 for llama) sat in the registry
with no carrier of any measure - no script ever shot them, and after any upstream sync the
registry silently lied; marker-provenance checks relied on a broken `git grep -l -F <token>` call
where a token starting with two dashes parsed as a flag (rc=129 read as "not in the base").

What changed?
- packaging/kit/ci/registry_counts.py (+243/-0): a new local measure - `merge-base` plus
  `rev-list --count --no-merges <base>..<head>` per engine, reconciling `commits_ours` and the base
  against live history while the head is reconciled with the commit named in the registry
  (`rev-parse --verify` plus `merge-base --is-ancestor`): a commit cannot carry its own hash, so
  comparing with the live tip would produce a false mismatch exactly on the commit that edits this
  registry; proving each marker from the "+" lines of `git show <commit>`, and
  refusing to call a marker ours when its name already lives in the upstream base tree; an empty
  marker list, a foreign head, a nonexistent commit, llama without the `--llama` flag and a repo
  without `.git` yield a mismatch or an exception with a reason instead of zero; `--selftest`
  prints 17 checks including six named sabotages.
- packaging/kit/ci/patch_markers.py (+81/-4): `snap_check` now holds the SHAPE of the number
  snapshot - six fields, hex 7-40 for base and head, a command naming merge-base / rev-list /
  --no-merges, a non-empty caveat and a YYYY-MM-DD date - and refuses to load the registry. A
  runner with `fetch-depth: 1` cannot re-shoot history, so the shape stays in the gate while the
  truth about the number stays local only. selftest adds 16 checks (2 shapes + 14 sabotages) and
  raises the floor from 24 to 40; the docstring names registry_counts.py instead of the
  nonexistent `ci_binary_markers2_2026-11-12.py`, and "all 72 commits verified" becomes "all our
  commits" - a number does not live in prose.
- packaging/kit/ci/patch-markers.json (+15/-5): `commits_ours` 81→89 (Strata) and 14→15 (llama),
  re-shot onto bases 13eedf552 / 81f21f4b2 and heads 8ca5f124 / 39628e5a4; every engine gained
  `commits_ours_cmd/base/head/at/note`, and the capture command walks from the base to the named
  head (`$b..8ca5f124`, `$b..39628e5a4`) instead of the live `main` / `kit-all-sync`: otherwise the

the runner, so the capture lives locally while the gate in the runner measures only marker
presence in the exe/dll bytes. The split had to be written down, otherwise the measure pretended

actions/checkout passes it to fetch as a ref name rather than a commit, so the
leg dies before the compiler is even invoked.

What changed?
- .github/workflows/kit-build.yml (+4/-1): GGML_PIN replaced with
  3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d, with a comment above the value
  carrying the action source citation and the exit-code measurement; the same
  tree is checked out under path ggml-pin via ref (:113).

  comment pointing at the expanded note in kit-build.yml; that pin is used in
  the ref of the same checkout step (:88).

The leg starts from the upstream ggml tree, whose K-quant templates close the
q2_k hole: without it CMake fails at generate step, which in the log is
indistinguishable from a broken toolchain. The pin was written with nine
characters, actions/checkout treats a short string as a ref name, fetch answers
«couldn't find remote ref», and the run turns red on the very first step -
before compilation, before the marker gates, with no mention of our patches.

Verified?
- git -C llama-3cf rev-parse 3cf03257f^{commit} -> rc=0 and the same hash as the
  full string: the pin really describes the needed tree, not a neighbouring commit.
- git fetch --depth 1 https://github.com/bahooo22/llama.cpp <full pin> -> rc=0,
  «branch ... -> FETCH_HEAD»; the same call with nine characters -> rc=128,
  «fatal: couldn't find remote ref 3cf03257f» - the sabotage control proving the
  defect was live rather than hypothetical.
- Primary source, raw actions/checkout@v4: input-helper.ts:92 accepts a commit
  only for strings matching /^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{40}|[0-9a-fA-F]{64})$/.
- YAML parsing (pyyaml safe_load): kit-build.yml -> jobs ['ci-gates',
  'strata-cuda'], 11 steps; kit-release.yml -> ['kit'], 13 steps; env.GGML_PIN is
  40 characters long in both; the llama fork leg (blob of branch kit-all-sync) ->
  ['llama-cuda'], 9 steps, containing no reference to this pin.
- packaging/kit/ci/patch_markers.py --selftest -> rc=0, ok=28 bad=0;
  packaging/kit/ci/verify_zip.sh --selftest with the explicit
  Git\bin\bash.exe -> rc=0, ok=6 bad=0. The first measurement of the same call
  resolved «bash» through PATH and returned rc=1 with execvpe(/bin/bash) failed:

EN: The zip gate prints its signature rejection with a single separator

The defect surfaced during the offline acceptance run of the automation: the byte-level format gate
was exercised over three inputs, and its rejection line read a doubled separator where the canonical
archive signature has one. The check itself behaved correctly - only the human-visible log text was
wrong.

What changed?
- packaging/kit/ci/verify_zip.sh (+1/-1): in the header-rejection message inside check_bytes the
  signature literal was written with two backslashes per separator, so bash expands it to a pair and
  the step log shows "PK, two separators, 3, two separators, 4". Replaced with single separators; the
  compared code 504b0304 and the rejection branches are untouched, and the neighbouring EOCD line
  (504b0506) did not change because it contains no separators. The comment above the function (:57)
  already spelled the signature with one separator, so the message now matches both the comment and
  the ci-artifact-format-gate skill.

Why?
The "byte-level archive format gate" step in kit-release.yml emits this rejection into Actions, and a
reader decides the cause from its wording: "this is not a zip, it is a posix-tar wearing a .zip
extension". A doubled separator looks like a typo in the archive bytes themselves, which injects doubt
into the very measurement that exists to distinguish our gate from the archiver's silent exit code. The
defect never blocked a green run, which is exactly why it survived until this measurement.

Verified?
Taken 2026-11-13 on the stand, three inputs, the exit code printed immediately after each measurement:
- corrupt input (posix-tar named .zip produced by the bare tar from Git for Windows): rc=1, "no header
  PK\3\4 (got 6770752d) - this is not a zip". Before the fix the same input produced the same branch
  with two separators per unit; 6770752d are the first four bytes of a posix-tar, not of a zip;
- real archive from the CI packaging rehearsal, dist/ci-rehearsal/gpu-infer-kit-ci-rehearsal.zip
  (831,231,811 bytes): rc=0, "25 entries, all 11 required records present";
- gate selftest: rc=0, ok=6 bad=0, including "tar-named-.zip rejected by signature", "partial archive
  rejected by content", "empty input gives rc=2", "truncated tail rejected".
- grep of the ci directory for doubled separators in messages: nothing besides the line fixed here -
  the other hits (kit_dll_deps.py, pack_kit.ps1, build_kit.ps1, install_cuda_redist.ps1) live inside
  regular expressions and PowerShell literal strings, where doubling is meaningful and never printed.
- numstat for this commit: git show --numstat --format= HEAD -> 1 path, +1/-1 (captured after the edit;
  the file has not changed since).

Accepted remainder?
The fix is cosmetic and changes no exit code on any input, so it does not wait on a live Actions run:
neither fork has a single kit-leg run because automation is disabled at the account level (the
dispatcher answers 422 while the repository-level permissions report enabled) - switching it on is the
owner's step. Run artifact formats, the marker registry and the kit layout are untouched by this change.

named by the same symbol the comment and the skill use for it, not by a doubled separator.

Before this change a reader building the kit from the README could not tell "the CI scripts are

The automation's readiness before the push now rests on three measurable gates written into the
README, and the difference between "verified offline" and "not yet run in Actions" is readable

EN: GH_TOKEN in the release asset upload step of the kit

Uploading the asset is the last action of the release leg: the archive is built, its format is
checked, and only then `gh` tries to put it into the release. Measured on 13.11 that without a
token in the step env this failure is certain: `gh` does not inherit the automatic run token even
though `contents: write` is declared earlier in the same file.

What changed?
- .github/workflows/kit-release.yml (+9/-0): the "Release asset upload" step got an env with a
  `GH_TOKEN` line taken from `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, plus a separate guard for an empty token -
  `::error::` with an explicit reason and rc=2. Both `gh` calls stand after the guard, so an empty
  token never pretends that the release is missing.
- packaging/kit/README.ru.md (+5/-1): the Russian entry of the same workflow list now names both
  the token requirement and the reason for rc=2.
- packaging/kit/README.en.md (+7/-2): the English mirror - the refusal must read as "the
  publication did not happen", not as "our patches are gone".

Why?
Before the edit the kit build spent both engines and the whole packaging and then died on the last
step with a message about an environment variable. Its exit code 1 is indistinguishable from
refusing to publish into a release that does not exist: a person reading the Actions log cannot
tell that the archive is intact and the patches are in place.

Verified?
YAML parsed after the edit (`yaml.safe_load`, local `main` on tree `37d34a9a`): 13 steps, the upload
step env = `{'GH_TOKEN': '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'}`, permissions = `{'contents': 'write'}`, the
empty-token guard is present in the step text. The token requirement for `gh` inside Actions was
checked against the GitHub docs. There is no live Actions run yet: `origin/main` holds neither
`packaging/kit/ci/` nor the two kit workflows - that is on the user (push, then the release tag).

Result
The asset upload now depends on the token explicitly, and an empty token returns its own rc=2 with
a reason; a death after a two-hour build no longer looks like "the patches are missing".

EN: ci: the marker gate checks registry numbers and attribution by topology

`patch-markers.json` survived the upstream syncs with its numbers still shot
from the older tree: coverage read "12 of 72" while the tree already carries 81
of our commits. Six attributions were false — a marker was credited to a commit
that merely mentions the name instead of the one that introduced it.

What changed?
- `packaging/kit/ci/patch-markers.json` (+31/-23): the extraction rule is now
  recorded in a `marker_rule` field for both legs; the stale `candidates` and
  `ours_unique` counters, read by nothing, are removed; `commits_ours` 72 → 81
  (Strata) and 12 → 14 (llama), `markers` 23 → 24 and 5, `commits_with_marker`
  llama 4 → 3; the `k_fa_prefill` marker is added (kind kernel, commit
  `cc4da32c`, carriers `strata-q36.exe` and `strata.exe`); six attributions
  re-taken: `STRATA_Q36_ATT_MB` `a00ab004` → `efec68e7`, `STRATA_Q36_FA_LAYER`
  `0b200472` → `cc4da32c`, `STRATA_Q36_SUPER_CHUNK` `0b200472` → `36dddeb1`,
  and `GGML_CUDA_UPLOAD_STREAM`, `GGML_MOE_TRACE` and `GGML_SCHED_COPIES` all
  onto `62d89edc2`.
- `packaging/kit/ci/patch_markers.py` (+16/-5): four new self-checks per leg —
  `markers` equals the list length, `commits_with_marker` equals the set of
  `commit` fields, coverage never exceeds `commits_ours`, and `marker_rule` is
  populated; the measure threshold rises from 14 to 24 checks; the comment
  above `ASCII_ONLY` is rewritten (it described something other than what the
  constant guards and carried a glued word); a `ПРОПАЛ` line with no hit
  carriers no longer prints as "found in nowhere".
- `packaging/kit/README.ru.md` (+10/-3): the gate paragraph now carries the
  actual numbers (24 Strata markers, 5 on the llama leg, 12 of 81 and 3 of 14
  commits).
- `packaging/kit/README.en.md` (+11/-3): the same mirror in English; both
  extraction rules are stated in either language.

Why?
A green Actions build does not prove our patches are present; the registry is
the only artifact that does. While its numbers were never cross-checked
against the marker list, the file could silently lie after every upstream
sync, and a false attribution would report "patch in place" for a marker
actually introduced by a different commit.

Verified
- Selftest on the final file: `python packaging/kit/ci/patch_markers.py
  --selftest` → `ok=28 bad=0`, rc=0 (taken 12.11).
- Mutation acceptance (`E:\tmp\pm_accept.sh`): `markers` 23 against a list of
  24 → `bad=1`, rc=1; `commits_with_marker` 17 against 12 → `bad=2`, rc=1; an
  empty `marker_rule` → `bad=1`, rc=1. The threshold of 24 keeps a truncated
  check block from going green.
- Gate over the kit tree (`E:\tmp\pm_final_gate_strata.sh`,
  `E:\tmp\pm_stock_control_2026-11-12.sh`): Strata `24/24`, commits `12 of 12`,
  rc=0; llama `5/5`, commits `3 of 3`, rc=0.
- Negative control with the same measure against a clean-upstream build
  (`llama-3cf/build-stock/bin`): `маркеров 0/5`, rc=1, all five tokens named —
  the gate does catch "Actions built the wrong tree".
- Attribution audit (`pm_attr_check_2026-11-12.py`) after the re-shoot: 0
  mismatches, 0 names that are not ours-only (found in the upstream base), 0
  new candidates.

Accepted remainder
`commits_ours` in the registry is a 12.11 snapshot and must be re-shot after
each upstream sync; marker coverage (12 of 81, 3 of 14) does not reach edits
that leave no readable name in a binary — those stay covered by parity
measurements on the bench. The live Actions run and the push remain with the
user.

Result
The registry can no longer lie quietly: numbers disagreeing with the marker
list and an empty extraction rule turn the self-check red, and a false
attribution is caught by the topology audit rather than by author dates.

DeepSeek gfx906: no huge-page request for the RAM copy of the experts - decode no longer freezes for seconds (28 tok/s in 20 runs of 20, was 8-20 in 4 of 10)

Asking for transparent huge pages for the 86 GB copy makes the kernel compact memory, and compaction moves pages of
the host memory the GPU driver has mapped (ROCm's pinned memory is userptr). Each move stops every queue of the
process until the pages are mapped again: a kernel trace showed both dies frozen 1-6 s at a time, 18 s in 256 tokens.
gfx906 builds only; DS4_ANON_THP=1 asks for huge pages again, =0 turns them off elsewhere.

RU: pack_kit: гейт переносимости ловит любой разделитель после литеры диска

Гейт «в тексте комплекта нет путей чужой машины» был зелёным при четырнадцати реальных
путях стенда, и ровно та же форма записи приходит с GitHub-раннера. Фикс расширяет
сигнатуру до «любая литера, любой разделитель» и закрывает её регрессиями.

Что изменено?
- packaging/kit/ci/pack_kit.ps1 (+33/-5): `$STAND_PATH_RE` был
  `(?i)([def]:\\|c:\\users\\)` — три литеры и только обратный слэш, тогда как
  `elf-proof.json` и `build-measure.json` пишут путь «литера, косая черта, дерево, а
  обратный слэш стоит перед именем файла»; шаблон на такой форме молчал. Теперь
  `(?i)(?<![a-z])[a-z]:[\\/]` (:66), lookbehind обязателен — без него `https://`
  совпадает на `s://`. Очистка идёт той же сигнатурой: `$pat` в `Remove-StandPaths`
  (:155) и свёртка совпадения в имя разрезом по `[\\/]` (:160), иначе косые черты
  давали ноль изменений в мере. Семь контроли в `-SelfTest`: косая черта после литеры
  тоже находка (:268), https-ссылка не находка (:272), свёртка косой (:318) и смешанного
  разделителя (:319), ссылка не изуродована очисткой (:320), вычищенная мера больше не
  находится гейтом (:324) и вычищенная ссылка цела (:325); формулировка пункта 2 в
  шапке (:19-20) переписана под «ни одной формы записи — ни стенда, ни раннера».
- packaging/kit/start.ps1 (+1/-1): пример в справке (:8) `C:\models\model.gguf` →
  `.\models\model.gguf` — текст обвязки тоже лежит в комплекте и попадает под строгий
  гейт, а исключение из правила «путей с литерой нет» для own-справки означало бы
  слабый гейт или вечную сноску.
- packaging/kit/README.ru.md (+19/-15): пункт 2 гейта (:132) — обе формы записи названы
  словами, без литеральных путей; абзац границы входа (:148-149) — pwsh 7 даёт `ok=73 bad=0`,
  5.1 — `ok=69 bad=4` (прежде 63/3), с оговоркой, что красное на 5.1 стоит на несостоявшемся
  входе: тестовое дерево не создаётся, `-Encoding utf8NoBOM` появился только в PowerShell 6+,
  и контроли, ждушие ноль, проходят вхолостую.
- packaging/kit/README.en.md (+18/-13): те же два места по-английски (:133-134, :151-152);
  нумерация строк в паре разная, якоря RU-оригинала перенесены зеркалом.

Зачем?
Комплект, собранный в Actions, обязан быть пригоден на чужой машине — это единственный
смысл слова «portable». Дырявый гейт пропускал архив, в котором сайдкары указывают на
каталог сборочной машины: пользователь получает комплект, чьи доказательства (какие
cubin внутри бинарника и какие библиотеки нужны) ссылаются на несуществующие пути, и ни одна
проверка при этом не краснеет. У GitHub-раннера рабочий каталог тоже начинается на
литере C (`D:/a/<repo>/<repo>/…` из CMake), то есть прогон в Actions собирал «зелёный»
комплект с четырнадцатью чужими путями внутри — дефект был не косметикой, а пропуском
в публикуемый ассет. Иначе нельзя было: расширение сигнатуры до «любой разделитель»

- Строгая мерка (`(?i)(?<![a-z])[a-z]:[\\/]`) по упакованному дереву до фикса: 14

  путей стенда в текстовых файлах нет», та же мерка по 12 текстовым файлам дерева = 0
  находок (замер 12.11, `E:\tmp\kit352_rehearsal.sh`).
- Раннерная форма входов (пути вида `D:/a/Strata/Strata/…`) подставлена в меры и

- Ложные срабатывания кандидата на живом дереве: 14 находок, ноль ложных. Время вида

- `-SelfTest`: pwsh 7 `ok=73 bad=0` (было 66), Windows PowerShell 5.1 `ok=69 bad=4`

- Мерка по исходникам обвязки (README.ru/en, start.ps1, START.bat, `*.py`,

- Доказательная сила мер после очистки не потеряна: `want_archs` = sm_86, sm_89, sm_120;

  a compilation. The ninja denominator `[N/M]` is the plan of the current call and cannot measure
  coldness.

  build" (0 objects before the run), "partial build" (after an edit), "no-op" (0 edges executed)
  and "coldness not measured" (`PreObjects = -1`, the parameter default).

or the build fails "strangely" and the marker gate measures carriers that are not there. The first
live run on 12.11 exposed two independent defects in the CI script that no earlier self-check saw.

What changed?
- packaging/kit/ci/install_cuda_redist.ps1 (+126/-22): a new Test-IndexJson decides index
  suitability by structure (release_label must equal -CudaVersion, at least 20 component entries,
  and a failed JSON parse reported separately); Save-Index calls it before parsing and prints
  "index is usable: N bytes"; the byte threshold `-lt 50000` is gone and a check over the script's
  own text catches its return. A new Merge-Into replaces the top-level Move-Item in
  Expand-RedistArchive: the archive tree is now merged recursively into the toolchain root. The
  per-component report carries files_moved instead of entries_moved, and the console prints
  "moved N files". The .DESCRIPTION now states the directory-overlap rule taken from a listing of
  the 9 archives (bin in 4 of 9, include in 6 of 9, lib in 3 of 9). -SelfTest: 16 Chk lines
  (15 executed, threshold 12) became 28 (27 executed, threshold 27) - seven checks for the merge of

  no bin\bin or include\include layer, the first archive's file intact, the lift finding both dll)
  and five for the index gate.

  index suitability and the recursive merge of the archive layout.
- packaging/kit/README.en.md (+14/-0): the same two paragraphs in the English mirror of that section.

Before this change a complete toolchain could not be built outside the bench: the "CUDA toolchain"
step aborted before the first download, because the live full redistrib_13.3.1.json weighs 47 914
bytes and failed a 50 000-byte threshold. Even if the index had passed, the toolchain would have
been incomplete: components share directories, and moving a directory onto an existing directory
makes PowerShell put it INSIDE - the live run produced bin\bin\x64\cublas64_13.dll,
bin\bin\cuobjdump.exe and include\include\cuda_runtime.h while all nine sha256 values matched.
Neither the hashes nor the number of moved entries saw this; only the mandatory file list in

- local ci-gates (five self-tests plus a YAML parse of the three workflows): "CI-GATES GREEN

- CI-faithful build build_kit.ps1 -Engines strata -Arch 86 -SkipProbe on this toolchain (12.11,

EN: CI: release workflow that builds and publishes the portable kit

The second automation pipeline: kit-build.yml covers pushes with one engine and one architecture,
which is enough to guard the patches but not to ship. This workflow builds the full kit and
publishes it as an asset of an already existing release.

What changed?
- `.github/workflows/kit-release.yml` (+232/-0): job `kit` on windows-2022,
  `timeout-minutes: 240` derived from the bench measurement in build-measure.json dated 12.11
  (strata 712.6 s + llama 2788.8 s), with headroom for the toolchain and packaging.
- Three tree inputs: `strata` (this fork), `llama` (fork `bahooo22/llama.cpp`, ref
  `kit-all-sync`) and `ggml-pin` (same fork pinned at `3cf03257f` for the K-quant
  template-instances, without it CMake fails at generate); foreign checkouts use
  `persist-credentials: false` so no run can push out of someone else's tree.
- "Inputs checked before compilation": 8 files (packaging/kit/ci/build_kit.ps1, pack_kit.ps1,
  kit_dll_deps.py, patch_markers.py, verify_zip.sh, packaging/kit/START.bat,
  ggml-pin/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mma.cuh, llama/CMakeLists.txt); a missing one prints
  `::error::нет $f - сборка не начата` and exits 2 — "the check did not happen", not "it broke".
- Toolchain: cache key `cuda-dl-${CUDA_VERSION}-kit` plus install_cuda_redist.ps1 into
  `RUNNER_TEMP\cuda` (the windows-2022 image has no CUDA, and the full distribution requires
  licence confirmation).
- `build_kit.ps1 -Engines 'strata;llama' -Arch 86;89;120 -SkipProbe`: only the paired run writes
  the merged build-measure.json / elf-proof.json, which is exactly what pack_kit.ps1 reads; single
  engines would leave *.partial.json and packaging would ship half of the proof. Here `-Arch`
  changes the archive contents, not just codegen width as in kit-build.yml.
- Byte-level marker gate for both legs: `patch_markers.py --engine strata` over strata-q36.exe and
  strata.exe, `--engine llama` over ggml-base.dll, ggml-cuda.dll, llama.dll; return codes
  accumulate into `$bad` and one aggregate `::error::маркеры потеряны в: …` exits 1 — a green build
  on its own proves nothing about our patches.
- `kit_dll_deps.py`: native import registry over six binaries (both strata executables,
  llama-server.exe, ggml-cuda.dll, ggml-base.dll, llama.dll); dumpbin is located through vswhere and
  its absence exits 2; the closure is checked against `cuda\bin` and `--extra-dir`
  llama\build-kit\bin, producing runtime-deps.json.
- `pack_kit.ps1 -StrataBuild -LlamaBuild -Measures -Stage -CudaBin`, with `-Version` appended only
  when `KIT_TAG` (`github.event.release.tag_name || github.event.inputs.tag`) is non-empty — the
  archive name and the tag come from one source of truth; without a tag the packer falls back to the
  start date from build-measure.json and the publish step is skipped.
- Archive format gate before publishing: bash array `files=( "$RUNNER_TEMP"/gpu-infer-kit-*.zip )`
  exiting 2 on zero or on several matches (which one to publish would be ambiguous), then
  verify_zip.sh on the PK\3\4 header and the EOCD signature, and the path is exported to
  `GITHUB_ENV` as `KIT_ZIP`. Under bash a bare tar writes a POSIX tar with exit code 0 and GitHub
  labels it application/zip by extension — without this gate a dead archive reaches the user.
- Run artifacts `kit-release-${{ github.run_number }}` with `if: always()`: the archive,
  build-measure.json, elf-proof.json, runtime-deps.json, markers-strata.json, markers-llama.json,
  build-strata.log, build-llama.log, kit-weight.json; retention 30.
- Publication: empty tag → "asset is not published" and exit 0; missing `KIT_ZIP` → exit 2;
  `gh release view "$KIT_TAG"` otherwise exit 1 (gh release upload does not silently create a
  release); then `gh release upload "$KIT_TAG" "$KIT_ZIP" --clobber` with a printed return code.
- `permissions: contents: write` (this job alone publishes) and `cancel-in-progress: false` — an
  hourly build must not be discarded by the next push.

Why?
The portable kit differs in composition from the push pipeline: it needs both engines, three
architectures and the DLL closure, and the user needs a release asset named after the tag rather
than a run artifact. Before this file the kit was assembled by hand on the bench and none of the
checks (patch markers, zip format, architecture coverage) were mandatory, so an incomplete kit or
one built from a clean upstream tree could ship.

Verified
- `bash glm/scripts/kit322_ci_automation_gate_2026-11-12.sh` (12.11, before the commit): the
  workflow check over three files and two trees printed its Russian verdict verbatim —
  `вход: workflow 3, строк 562, путей проверено 15, деревьев 2, находок 0` and `WORKFLOW GATE OK`;
  the mutation control of the measure itself printed `selfcheck workflow-меры: ok=5 bad=0`
  (real workflow rc=0, misspelled script name rc=1, unquoted `name:` rc=1, missing file rc=2,
  empty file rc=2).
- `python -X utf8 leakcheck.py --prose` over the three workflow files (12.11): verbatim `Чисто.`, rc=0.
- The paired `-Engines 'strata;llama'` run and the packaging in Actions have not been executed:
  push and CI approvals belong to the user, and there are no GPU runners.

Accepted remainder
The live kit-release.yml run (workflow_dispatch without a tag for build plus artifact, then with a
release tag for the asset upload) is pending, since it needs a push and a build approval. Per-arch
cost probes (`-ProbeScript`) and running the servers with a model are absent here for the same
reason as in kit-build.yml and are printed as skips in the header.

Result
The kit release is now one run with two mandatory gates — patch markers verified byte-wise on both
legs and the archive format verified by signature — published as an asset only into an existing release.

артефактом даже при красном результате.
