EN: CI: build and packaging scripts for the portable kit

Plan 11-12.11, part 4.6. These seven scripts are what the bench used to build the two-engine
tree and pack it into gpu-infer-kit, but they were not in history: without them a GitHub Actions
run is not reproducible, and there was nothing at all to check that "the built exe really carries
our patches". They are in the repository now - with no bench paths: every input is either a
parameter or a named refusal.

What changed?
- packaging/kit/ci/build_kit.ps1 (+998/-0): builds Strata and llama.cpp for a list of
  architectures in one call. Inputs -StrataSrc/-LlamaSrc/-Out/-Cuda/-Engines/-Arch; a missing
  mandatory parameter refuses with its own name and rc=2; `-Engines 'starta'` catching no engine
  is rc=2 too, otherwise the binary list would be empty and the "proof" would look like a run.
  `Assert-FreshCache` rejects a relocated CMake cache (compilation would otherwise run out of
  someone else's tree), `Get-BuildWork` counts compiles and links from the log,
  `Set-EngineMeasure` records the carrier commit, timings and sizes, and `Get-ArchProofMap`
  proves architectures by fact - `cuobjdump --list-elf` per binary. A single engine writes its
  measures with the `.partial.json` suffix and never touches the merged files: a partial measure
  mistaken for a full one would silently zero the architecture coverage.
- packaging/kit/ci/pack_kit.ps1 (+622/-0): copies the tree per `Get-Manifest` and runs six gates
  before an archive counts as ready: every mandatory file exists; no bench paths in text files
  (`Test-NoStandPaths`); the three sidecars parse as JSON without BOM (`Read-JsonNoBom` measures
  the first byte, because content with a BOM also "looks like JSON" while kit\classify.py
  json.loads fails on it); the architecture proof covers what is claimed and the dependency
  closure is complete; the zip opens, its entry count matches the tree, and it contains no model
  files; folder and zip weight is measured, not estimated (`Get-TreeBytes`).
  `Test-StageSafe`/`Test-StageOwn` forbid Stage inside Measures or on top of foreign files.
- packaging/kit/ci/patch_markers.py (+283/-0): the patch gate over binary bytes. Two token
  classes - string literals (env vars, CLI flags, error texts) and CUDA kernel names from the
  fatbin; the compiler does not keep local function names, so commits without such a trace are
  not in the registry. A missing carrier is rc=2 (part of the patches unchecked), a vanished
  marker is rc=1; `commits_covered` counts covered commits.
- packaging/kit/ci/patch-markers.json (+315/-0): the registry itself: Strata has 23 markers over
  12 of our 72 commits (carriers strata-q36.exe and strata.exe), llama has 5 markers over 4
  commits (ggml-base.dll, ggml-cuda.dll, llama.dll), each with its commit and subject.
- packaging/kit/ci/kit_dll_deps.py (+327/-0): native import registry via `dumpbin /imports` plus
  the dependency closure: every imported DLL must resolve in CUDA\bin, System32 or a passed
  directory, otherwise it is listed and rc=1. The list survives a CUDA version bump - a newly
  imported DLL shows up in the measure, not when the kit fails to start on someone else's
  machine.
- packaging/kit/ci/install_cuda_redist.ps1 (+346/-0): builds the CUDA toolchain from NVIDIA
  redist archives - no installer, no multi-gigabyte full distribution: $PINS pins a sha256 per
  component, `Get-CudaDefaults` returns exactly 9 (nvrtc and nvjitlink excluded), each archive is
  laid out at the toolchain root and DLLs are lifted from bin\x64 to bin - as on the bench, so
  the nvcc built here behaves like the bench one.
- packaging/kit/ci/verify_zip.sh (+160/-0): a format gate over the archive bytes rather than the
  packer's exit code: PK\3\4 header and EOCD 504b0506 exactly 22 bytes before the end, bsdtar
  listing normalized for CRLF and backslashes, a minimum entry count, 11 required paths, no
  *.gguf inside. Codes 0/1/2 are distinct: an empty or missing input means "the check did not
  happen", not "all clean".

Why?
A portable kit can only be published as a release asset if it is built from history. While the
measures lived in a directory outside the repository, "the built server carries our patches"
could be neither reproduced nor challenged: on another machine the archive opened fine and the
missing patch surfaced only through engine behaviour.

Verified?
Selftest gate - `bash glm/scripts/kit322_ci_selftest_gate_2026-11-12.sh` on the bench, 2026-11-12;
the toolchain and GPU are not needed for it:
  - build_kit.ps1 -SelfTest - 88/88 checks passed;
  - pack_kit.ps1 -SelfTest - ok=66 bad=0;
  - install_cuda_redist.ps1 -SelfTest - ok=15 bad=0;
  - patch_markers.py --selftest - ok=20 bad=0;
  - verify_zip.sh --selftest - ok=6 bad=0;
  - summary: ok=5 bad=0, SELFTEST GATE OK, rc=0.
Leak scan over the seven files (`glm/scripts/kit322_ci_scan_2026-11-12.sh`, leakcheck 1.0.0):
7 files, 0 with findings, 0 failed checks. Before the scan, four defects of my own text were
fixed: probe file names `нет-такого.json`/.bin/.zip glued Cyrillic to Latin across a dot
(renamed to missing.*), the kit_dll_deps.py docstring invoked itself by a path outside the
repository (now `python packaging/kit/ci/kit_dll_deps.py ...`), and references to archive
measures in pack_kit.ps1 and install_cuda_redist.ps1 now name the sibling file in the same
folder.

Accepted remainder?
The full live run of these scripts on CUDA hardware was not measured in this commit - it has to
happen in GitHub Actions (the workflow and release-asset tasks), and only there will it become
visible that the exe and dll built in Actions pass the marker gate. Pushing is the user's call.

Result
Build, packaging and the three measures (byte-level markers, DLL closure, zip format) now live in
history and run from it; every script input is either supplied or named in the refusal, and a
falsely green run is separated from a real failure by rc=2.

dsv41: --expert-cache-device1 fills CUDA1 with the CPU lane's experts

A second card that takes layers runs every token through them one after
the other, so a small or slow card slows the larger one.  With
--expert-cache-device1 N|auto (the Qwen engine's flag for its helper
caches) CUDA1 takes no layers: it holds the experts the layer cards left
to the CPU lane, the most-routed first by the profile's share of their
layer across all layers, N of them or as many as fit beside
--reserve-mib and 256 MiB for its decode buffers.  Each layer gets a
host map (expert -> slot) and a device table of slot addresses on
CUDA1; the bytes come from read_mx through pinned staging.  The CPU lane
keeps its copies, and decode does not use CUDA1 yet.  The start-up
summary names the experts, their bytes and their share of the routed
picks by the profile.

dsv41: CUDA1 computes its experts' part of a decode token

With --expert-cache-device1 the service thread hands CUDA1 the picks of
a decode token (a window of one) whose experts it holds: the token's FFN
input, ids and weights go to CUDA1, card_plan_k makes the plan from the
layer's CUDA1 table, the GGUF expert kernels (gg::moe_gate_up /
moe_down) sum them, and the part comes back to pinned memory, all on
CUDA1's stream while the CPU lane computes the rest.  The service thread
then adds it to the CPU lane's part (or makes it the part) before it
publishes the answer, so the main card's kernels and its wait stay as
they were.

The lanes keep their order: the main card's VRAM, the RAM store's
zero-copy (the device's own choice), CUDA1, the disk skip, the CPU lane.
Windows of more than one token stay with the CPU lane.  A CUDA error on
CUDA1 stops the engine with a message.  DS4_CACHE_CARD=0 leaves CUDA1's
experts unused.  The serve log adds CUDA1's share of the experts and the

With --expert-cache-device1, when the main card's expert cache swaps in
an expert that CUDA1 holds, CUDA1's copy only takes a slot: the VRAM
lane comes first.  Between windows, where the main card's swaps are
switched, that slot is freed (CUDA1's table entry cleared) and

keeps the size of its layer's experts).  cc_th reads the expert from the
model file into pinned staging and copies it in on a copy stream of its
own, so decode does not wait for it; the expert is marked on its way
(-2) and stays with the CPU lane until a later tick puts it into the
tables.  A refill whose expert the main card took meanwhile frees the
slot again.  load_cache_card keeps each slot's address and layer for

The product never starts a debugger: every child it starts gets GGML_NO_BACKTRACE=1

ggml's abort path forks gdb (then lldb, then backtrace_symbols) to print a backtrace. On a launch onto a card another program had filled, gdb attached to the crashing picture reader, wrote its own errors into the reader's output and the engine log, and the launch ended with "Couldn't get registers: No such process" instead of the cause.

The fork's code does not rebase on pancake, so none of it is copied:
- its window kernel is a SPLIT instance of the fork's dense int8 prompt_attn_dense_kernel, which pancake does not
  have (pancake's QSA prompt kernels take a selection id list);
- its only callers are the main engine's verify / MTP paths when there is no indexer (qwen35moe on the fork's main
  engine). pancake's main engine runs only Flash-Next, which always has the QSA indexer; qwen35moe goes to
  src/qwen35 (strata's family switch) or strata-poly;
- its guard needs 8 query heads per KV head; Flash-Next has 12 (24 / 2);
- the gain needs attention bytes that grow with context. Flash-Next's QSA reads at most 2,051 cells a row at any
  length; attention is 0.74 ms of a 24.8 ms window (3.0%) and latency-bound (c19f82b53), STRATA_ATTN_WMMA was
  neutral (8860719dd). Sharing K/V among a window's rows there needs the union of their own top-k selections:
  ceiling ~1% of decode. Not built.

What was ported: the idea, to the engine that has the fork's shape. pancake's Qwen3.6 engine (q36_engine.cu, the
7900 XT's Qwen3.6 path) runs dense attention, 16 query heads over 2 KV heads, head dim 256, MTP verify windows of up
to 8 rows, and its k_attn_part reads every 256-cell K/V chunk once per row and query head (8 T times per KV head for
a T-row window, FP32 cache). STRATA_ATTN_WINDOW=1 launches k_attn_window<8, NR> instead: one block per (chunk, KV
head, pair of rows) computes the 16 (row, head) pairs' partials with each K and V row loaded once (decode step: 1
read per chunk instead of 8; 3-row window: 2 instead of 24; 8 rows: 4 instead of 64). Partials in k_attn_part's
layout, k_attn_merge unchanged. One source for CUDA and HIP (no warp intrinsics, 32 KB static LDS, 256 threads).
Only one session's rows (batch rows keep k_attn_part) and the 8-per-KV-head, 256-dim shape. Unset: the old launch,
unchanged, so the default is byte-identical.

Exactness: designed to be bit for bit k_attn_part, not rounding-level (the fork's kernels are rounding-level): the
same per-pair q.k order (i ascending, `a += q * k`), `s = a * scale`, block_max's and block_sum's shared-memory trees
replayed per pair over the same thread -> cell map, `e = expf(s - m)`, the V sum over the row's cells ascending.
Host emulation (not a GPU run): both kernels compiled together for the CPU (256 std::threads a block, a barrier for
__syncthreads, static locals as shared memory) give bitwise equal acc, m and l in 6 cases (T 1-5, 1-2 KV heads,
chunk-edge rows, a dead and a live row in one block, odd T, NaN in every cell past the window and never read), with
-ffp-contract=fast and =off. Open on the GPU: nvcc / hipcc must make the same contraction choice for `a * scale`
feeding `expf(s - m)` in both kernels. Check per backend (MOD_PLAN F11 status, step 1): strata-q36
--dump-full-logits with and without the switch, cmp equal (also --mtp 2 and --no-graph). If not equal: rounding-
level, token forcing + KL gate (tools/qwen35/kl.py) before any preset.

gfx1100 matrix-core version (design only, would be STRATA_ATTN_WINDOW=2, rounding-level; full text in MOD_PLAN):
- v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16, not the iu8 form: on gfx1100 both do 16x16x16 per instruction at the same rate, so int8
  buys no MACs (the fork used IMMA because sm_80+ runs it at 2x HMMA); f16 keeps FP32 accumulation and takes int8
  codes / fp16 values exactly as B. FP32 cache: q and K as fp16 hi + lo, 3 WMMAs a k-step (qh.kh + ql.kh + qh.kl);
  with an fp16 cache (follow-up STRATA_Q36_KV16, half the bytes) 2, B exact.
- M-tile = 8 heads x 2 rows (16 pairs, the fork's small-window tile), NT = ceil(T/2) <= 4, so all T x 8 <= 64 pairs
  of a KV head go in ONE pass (the exact kernel needs a pass per 2 rows); N = 16 cells, K = 16 dims; 4 waves per
  workgroup on (KV head, range of chunks), persistent.
- 32-cell sub-chunks: K hi/lo in LDS (32 KB), S (8 KB), P hi/lo (8 KB), then V transposed into K's space (~48 KB);
  q hi/lo A fragments from a pre-split fp16 image in global (BFLA's Q-from-global was 11% faster on this card).
- Online softmax inside each 256-cell chunk so each chunk still ends with k_attn_part's (m, l, acc) and k_attn_merge
  stays; DPP row reductions; P.V with wave w owning dims 64w..64w+63 (NT x 4 x 8 accumulators, <= 128 VGPRs).
- 3-row window at 128K (estimate): K + V 512 MB per layer once (0.64 ms at 800 GB/s) vs 2 reads for the exact
  kernel; ~25 GFLOP of WMMA per layer with the splits (~0.25 ms): bandwidth-bound, the splits are free.
- Decode steps must take the same kernel as windows (verify row = decode row, the engine's MTP rule); token forcing

- Flash-Next form (union of the rows' QSA selections, row masks, ATTN_WMMA's int8 arithmetic): not recommended,

same order. Float addition is commutative, so after every level both partners

[Engine] A4 rank-guard fix: STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU_FOLD (one pool pass when few rows are deferred)

With STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU (and its weight split, _BELOW 0.1 by default) a
deferred layer runs two CPU pool passes: the heavy jobs, then the partial flag,
then the light jobs whose rows join one layer late.  The rank guard (_TOP=2)
makes more jobs heavy, so many layers end up with a second pass over one or two
light experts (test phase 01: _TOP=2 +20.1% edit but -6.9% short chat).

STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU_FOLD=<n> (default off): a layer with at least one heavy
job and at most n light jobs runs all of them in one pass and raises the partial
flag after it.  Exact with respect to the same _TOP/_BELOW run: post(l) and
late_add pick their rows on the GPU by the weight rule (copy_rows_by_weight),
not by the pass that wrote them, and the pool cuts every phase by output rows,
so a row's value does not depend on the pass.  Only timing changes (post(l)
also waits for the folded light rows).  Unset: the code path and the log are

serve: STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE, park the deepest checkpoint prefix that fits

Parking refused whole: when the outgoing chain does not fit the cache byte
budget or the physical-RAM floor, the whole snapshot was dropped and the next
request of that conversation re-read its prompt from the root.  With
STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE=1 the chain's checkpoints are walked deepest-first and the
first prefix that passes both gates is parked instead: the copy keeps root +
chain + K/V [0, L), and live mounts on that checkpoint's running state.  The
next request re-reads only the tail.  Single-stage only.

The eviction side mirrors it: an oldest unpinned entry under byte or RAM
pressure is shrunk to one of its own checkpoints before it is dropped whole
(not below --conversation-cache-min-tokens; never a pinned or guarded entry;
never one with a background copy or device-slot copy in flight).

Ported from TwoAnts/Strata 5ef4fc8b4b, adapted to pancake: the constructor takes
the indexer block and the switch; live.gdn is joined (live_pending) and
live.dev_tag cleared before the running state is replaced.

Off unless STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE is set to a value other than 0; default
behaviour is unchanged.  Not built or run in this change.

What this changes is the shape, not the choice.  One warp per token: lane j reads experts j, j+32, ...
(coalesced instead of a serial walk), the warp reduces to the best logit in a shuffle tree, and the
ranks are still visited in order, because a swap changes the set already picked.  The choice is the
same bits: a strictly greater logit wins, the smallest expert index breaks ties, the already-picked
test runs against the ids as they are at that rank, a token with no swap keeps the router's weights
untouched, and the softmax is the same expression.

timeout due returns 0 first - the same answer the loop below gives - so the driver is called only to serve a layer,

telemetry: the Monitor's PCIe tile had no link for AMD cards on Linux

_Nvml.read() reports pcie_gen, pcie_gen_max, pcie_width and the two
throughput counters; _Amd.read() (the amdgpu sysfs reader from #301)
reports none of them, so on Linux the Monitor's PCIe tile shows only
dashes while the NVIDIA tile fills in.

This adds the link the card actually gets: the narrowest and slowest hop
between the root port and the card, from each hop's max_link_speed and
max_link_width.  A card that negotiates Gen4 on its own hop but sits
behind a Gen3 root port really runs at Gen3, and that is the number a
bandwidth budget needs.  pcie_own_gen keeps the card's own hop aside so
the gap is visible, and pcie_path reports how many hops could be read --
the bottleneck is only claimed when all of them could, because a kernel
or a container that hides part of /sys/devices would otherwise report the
card's own hop as the whole path.

Measured on one MI50 32 GB in a Gen3 x16 slot (lspci: the root port at
00:02.0 runs at 8 GT/s x16, the bridge above the card is downgraded, and
the card's own hop negotiates 16 GT/s), /metrics reports pcie_gen 3,
pcie_gen_max 3, pcie_own_gen 4, pcie_width 16 and pcie_path 4/4.

Throughput is deliberately left out: amdgpu's pcie_bw is three counters
whose documented use is a total, not a direction, while _Nvml's
pcie_rx_mb is receive-only, so filling that name from pcie_bw would
label a combined figure as one direction.  Happy to follow up separately
if you want the tile to show a rate.

Conversation cache: --conversation-cache-min-tokens parks only conversations of at least N tokens

Parking happens on a switch and every parked conversation costs one of
--conversation-cache-slots whatever its length.  A client that interleaves
short side requests (an agent's tool-result follow-ups, often under 1k tokens)
with one long conversation therefore spends the cache on the side requests and,
once it is full, evicts the long one oldest-first - the reuse it wanted.

one 19,198-token conversation interleaved with three ~700-token requests, then
the same conversation again:

  min 12288  skip parking (703 tokens, below the 12288 minimum) x3
             re-send L: 19193 reused + 5 read in 135 ms      (wall 0.3 s, 304x)

The default 0 keeps the previous behaviour, so nothing changes without the flag:
wants() answers for the length alone and the gate stays enabled() && wants(),
exactly as the existing byte-budget and RAM-floor skips are.  The check runs
before make_room(), so a skipped park neither evicts nor stores anything, and it
returns the same non-error path those skips take.

HIP gfx12: native int8-WMMA prompt experts on gfx1200/gfx1201 (opt-in STRATA_PF_FUSED=1, #1277)

The native IQ / K-quant prompt-expert kernels (moe_fused_iq.cu,
native_w11_kernel) were gfx11-only; on RDNA4 a pack with
STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 silently kept the MMQ path.  They now compile and run
on gfx1200 / gfx1201.  Still opt-in: STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 stays off by
default (it changes rounding, so it is not an arch_defaults switch), and
STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE=0 still turns the native kernels off.

Compile gating
- STRATA_NAT_W12 for __gfx1200__ / __gfx1201__, STRATA_NAT_WMMA for
  either family.  The kernel calls the _gfx12 spelling of the iu8 WMMA
  builtin (the un-suffixed one does not compile there).  Any other
  target keeps the trapping body.

Kernel (same arithmetic, other lane layout)
- gfx12 WMMA fragments are 8 int8 per lane and the two lane halves hold
  different k (8*hi .. 8*hi+7), not a replica as on gfx11: B and A are
  loaded as uint2 at the matching offsets, and every 16-value k step is
  still one WMMA, so the per-16 scales of the IQ2_S / IQ2_XS paths are
  untouched.
- A lane's 8 accumulator rows are consecutive (8*hi + i), so a feature's
  gate and up are in the same lane: SwiGLU needs no __shfl_xor, and the
  down tile is stored as two float4 per lane.  NW_DROW(i, hi) gives the
  row of element i for the per-row scales.

Host side
- gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma(): exact gfx1200 / gfx1201 match, never a
  prefix, like the gfx11 helper.
- dev_info() takes the gfx11 list or gfx12, and also checks that the
  kernel the build loaded is the real one: the trap stub (a
  gfx12-generic or SPIR-V build on a listed card) declares no LDS and
  still passes hipFuncGetAttributes and the occupancy query.
- native_supported() reads the STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 opt-in itself:
  fused::available() / requested() belong to the Q2_0 pack's
  expert_w11_kernel, which is not ported and stays false on gfx12.  Off
  gfx12 the result is what it was.  prefill.cpp fused_ring() follows:
  a native pack asks native_supported() alone (it implied enabled()
  before), so on gfx12 it gets the fused buffer layout and ring.
- Grid factor per format: gfx12 holds 3 blocks per WGP for IQ2_S / IQ2_XS
  gate/up (LDS and VGPRs), 4 for the rest.  The occupancy API cannot say
  (it models 64 KB of LDS per multiprocessor), so it is a small table;
  STRATA_PF_OCC_W=N overrides it.  gfx11 keeps 4.
- experts_native() refuses a dm that is not 16-byte aligned on gfx12
  (the float4 stores); the prompt path's buffers always are.
- moe_fused.cu compares the gfx11 list with the helper instead of the
  "gfx11" prefix (no change on any listed part).

Tests (prefill_fused_iq_test)

sycl: publish the doorbell with the uncached write hint

The decode handshake publishes a ring sequence the host polls while the
window graph still runs. On an Arc (xe) a system-scope atomic store, even
with a release fence, is served from the GPU's cache and reaches the host
only when the kernel ends, so a host polling mid-window never sees the
ring. That is why the verify window had to wait for the whole graph
(STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST) and every expert had to be device-resident or in
the pinned mirror.

STRATA_DOORBELL_ATOMIC_LOAD already fixes the load side the same way; this
does the store side with the Intel uncached L1+L3 write hint. The release
fence stays (ordering only: a later payload store follows the ring).

Measured with sycl/probe/doorbell_store.cpp on an Arc A770: the host sees
the store at 230 ms with the kernel running to 2030 ms; with the old atomic
store it sees it at 2038 ms, exactly when the kernel ends (exit code 3).
-DSTRATA_DOORBELL_ATOMIC_STORE restores the atomic store.

This is a prerequisite for running with the CPU expert pool on xe (the
per-layer handshake); it does not by itself fix longer-prompt prefill.

prefill chunks ran to completion with no prefill failure (prompt reads

are correct is a separate, still-open issue: the base port has no doorbell

sycl: add the doorbell payload checksum

The decode handshake publishes a payload (the layer's activations, the
routed expert ids and weights) and then rings a sequence number the host
polls. The fences alone do not order the ring after the payload stores:
measured on an Arc A770, 14 of 2,832 rings in one run became visible
before the last activation store, so the CPU expert pool sometimes
computed on a partly stale payload. This is the fix the port's own
comments call for (elementwise.hpp: "the host can observe the ring and
then read a payload that has not landed").

The publish kernels now write, next to the sequence number, the ring it
belongs to and a checksum of the payload (the wrapping sum of every 32-bit
word mixed with its position, murmur3's finalizer - a plain sum missed a
reordering, [3,7] -> [7,3], of the expert ids) in a per-ring slot modulo 4,
and the payload is stored with the uncached write hint (a plain store to
host USM reaches the host only when the kernel ends on xe). The host waits
for the whole payload (doorbell_wait_payload) before the pool reads it, in
session_loop and both verify-window loops; the checksum is accepted in
either publish shape (with or without the routing weights), so a variant's
choice need not be plumbed to the reader. The sequence word grows from 1 to
9 mapped words (layer.cpp, verify.cpp) and the ring slot is reset with it.

Note this is a robustness fix, not the cure for the A770's garbage on
longer prompts: that one repros with every expert device-resident (no CPU
handshake) and points at oneMKL's >4 GiB operand bug, which needs the BLAS
staging the CUDA/HIP shims have.

sycl: stage oneMKL GEMM operands that lie more than 4 GiB into their allocation

oneMKL's GEMM reads the last, partial tile of an operand from the wrong
place when that operand lies more than 4 GiB into its device allocation
(measured on an Arc A770, oneMKL 2026.1: a BF16 B past 4 GiB gave its last
21 columns wrong, none below 4 GiB). The prompt path's GEMMs meet this:
their buffers come from the top of the multi-GiB expert cache / prefill
region. This is the leading explanation for the A770's garbage on prompts
longer than a few dozen tokens - it repros with every expert
device-resident, so it is not the CPU handshake.

Register every big device allocation (malloc_device_guarded, and the
segmented expert cache's reserved VA) in a small registry, add
device_offset_end(ptr, bytes), and in Gemm::bf16 / Gemm::f16 copy either
operand into a scratch buffer of the queue's own (a fresh allocation, so
at offset 0) when its end lies past 4 GiB, then run the GEMM on the staged
operand. STRATA_SYCL_GEMM_NO_STAGE=1 is the negative control.

Not validated end to end: the run that showed the garbage was an
all-resident mirror, which no longer fits in this machine's RAM, and the
runnable --mmap-experts config crashes on this A770 with or without the
staging (exit 139, UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST - verified a separate,
pre-existing fault with the negative control), so the staging has not yet
been shown to change an answer.

sycl: fix the GEMM staging scratch lifetime and unregister freed allocations

Follow-up to the >4 GiB GEMM staging.

- gemm_stage freed its scratch as soon as a larger operand arrived, but the
  in-order queue is asynchronous: a previous staged GEMM could still read the
  buffer.  Wait for the queue before the free.
- The staging used dpct::get_in_order_queue() while the GEMM runs on the
  descriptor's queue (strata::q_of(stream_)); pass the descriptor's queue so
  the copy is ordered before the GEMM for a non-default stream, and so two
  Gemm objects on different queues do not share the thread_local scratch.
- Staging that could not allocate fell silently back to the direct (wrong)
  GEMM; it now says so.
- device_alloc_map had no unregister, so a freed cache base left a stale
  entry that device_offset_end could mis-attribute after the VA was reused.
  Add device_alloc_unregister and call it where the expert cache frees base_.

#606: clamp the three unclamped q8_1 scale/sum emit sites via q8_1_ds

Three kernels still emit the (d, sum) pair of a q8_1 activation block
with a raw make_half2(d, sum), bypassing the finite helper the rest of
the tree uses (q8_1_finite.hpp, from 19de7f4 / f6601bf):

  fused_gr.cu   gr_q8_tail                 - the fused gate-reduce tail (QFUSE)
  verify_kernels.cu  gdn_q8_1_store        - the batched GDN verify store (QFUSE)
  iq_kernels.cu  s26_swiglu_q8_1_kernel   - the S26 swiglu path

A block whose amax overflows (or that reads a non-finite input) emits
d = inf/NaN; fp16 makes the pair NaN (or the pathological (0,0)). Nothing
downstream tests for it: a NaN scale poisons the fp16 dot of the quantized
activation and every sum downstream of it, and a fully non-finite logit
row ends at the sampler's all-NaN fallback - vocabulary id 0, the '!'
face of the degeneration reported in #606. Same defect class already
fixed at the other emit sites; these three were missed.

q8_1_ds() clamps both halves into the fp16-finite range (finite d,
non-negative finite sum - the sum is a mean of |x|), producing for the
GPU paths the same bits the CPU pool and the clamped GPU sites produce
for the same block. A clamp at the producer, content-blind: nothing
downstream of it is model-text-aware.

calibrate: the sweep visits every value in every round instead of once

Phase 1 measures each PCIe share once and takes the maximum, with the three prompts of that rate all at the one
setting.  Neighbours cannot be ordered that way: on this box 0.75 through 0.95 come out at 72.7, 69.0, 71.0 and
71.9, which is 0.2% apart, while the same settings moved 8-28% between engine starts.  A value that was worth a
real gain can lose its single sample and never be measured again, because phase 1's winner is the share phase 2
then sweeps spec_min_p at, and the confirm step only puts that one resulting pair against the default.

sweep() measures every value SWEEP_ROUNDS times inside the one engine start, one round visiting all of them and
every other round in reverse order, and the winners come from the medians.  Drift inside a sweep then lands on
every value the same number of times, and one bad sample cannot decide.  The same function runs phase 2, and the
confirm step uses the same round count instead of its own.

Cost: the sweep multiplies by SWEEP_ROUNDS, 3 by default.  A rate is three prompts of 128 tokens, so on this box
(six values, 95-100 tok/s) phase 1 goes from about 40 s to about 120 s, on a run that already loads the model more
than once.  A machine whose two leaders stay inside each other's noise can raise the constant.

Not in this change: phase 4 needs a restart per worker count and stays sequential, so a count is still taken from
one measurement each.

calibrate: the PCIe share sweep reaches 1.0, where no expert goes to the CPU pool

PCIE_FRACS stops at 0.75, so setup --calibrate never measures the value that takes the CPU pool out of the decode
window completely. 1.0 is a separate operating point rather than 0.75 carried further: the share is applied as
m = (nmiss * pcie_num) >> 8, so at any value below 1.0 at least one miss still goes to the CPU pool, and only at
1.0 does every non-resident expert come over PCIe. A CPU expert sits on the layer's critical path while the GPU
waits for it, and on a slow CPU that is the whole difference.

On a Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus with an RTX 5090 Laptop on PCIe 5.0 x16, 0.55 gives 51.1 tok/s against 71.3 at 1.0,
with cpu_exp falling from 1.06 to 0.00 per layer-window and the window time falling by the 11.3 ms of PCIe waiting
plus the CPU's expert time. A sequential sweep puts 1.0 at 78.8 against 72.7 for 0.75 and 51.5 for 0.35.

0.9 is added beside 1.0 so a machine where 1.0 is too much gets an interior point. pick() keeps the default unless a
candidate beats it by MIN_GAIN, so this cannot make a calibration worse. The cost is one rate per value, about 8 s
here.

split: the auto placement sees each stage's PCIe link

The miss cost (190 ms per unit of routed mass, fitted on x16 links) is one
constant for every stage, so --layer-split auto cannot see an asymmetric
pair: on 2x 4090 D with CUDA1 on a physical x1 link (1.6 GB/s measured) it
gives that card 26 layers (K=22) and reads a 29K prompt at ~350 tok/s.

Probe each stage's link inside the search (probe_pcie_h2d_gbps; the
stage-setup probes are skipped when --pcie-frac is given, and the search
needs the reading either way) and scale that stage's miss term by
clamp(20 GB/s / bw, 1, 64).  20 GB/s is pcie_frac_for_gbps' x16 reference;
the lower clamp keeps a symmetric machine on the exact formula the sweep's
K was fitted with (every scale 1.0 -> the objective is unchanged).

With it, auto picks the fit-in-cache boundary on that machine (K=38: the
narrow card's cache holds all of its layers' pairs, zero streaming there)
and reads the same prompt at ~1410 tok/s, ~4x.

The 190 ms mixes the decode CPU-pool cost with the prompt link cost;
scaling the whole per-stage term is the first-order fix (splitting the
constant would need a fresh fit on both a narrow and a wide link).

The engine's GEN line takes pin=N: the first N prompt tokens are a shared read-only prefix (a long document many

serve: STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1 prints the MTP drafts tested and accepted by depth for each request

spec: probabilistic draft acceptance for sampled MTP drafts (opt-in STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1)

Speculative rejection sampling for the MTP drafts of a sampled request. The draft layer samples
its draft from the chain's distribution q (its own Philox stream, counter | 1<<61) and writes
q's (id, probability) list; the verify head computes the target's post-chain p per row from the
split sampler's block lists (penalties, top_k, top_p, min_p, temperature; at most 64 entries)
and accepts draft d with min(1, p(d)/q(d)), else samples the residual max(0, p - q) with its
own uniform. Row t writes the draft on an accept and the residual sample (never d) on a reject,
so the host's accept loop and the commit are unchanged. Rows past the MTP drafts (a lookup
chain's tail) and suffix windows are point masses: accept with p(d), residual p without d - no
q never means q = 0 (the llama.cpp #29924 class). Greedy requests never reach the new kernels;
the nine existing sampler kernels keep identical SASS.

expert profile: refuse a header version other than 1, naming both numbers and the file

read_expert_profile read the header's version field and then ignored it
((void) version), so a profile of a later format would have been read as a
version 1 layout: the fields after the version are only known to be
n_layers, n_expert, slots, n_ranked in a version 1 file.  Refuse any other
version right after the magic, before the geometry check, with the version
found, the version this engine reads, and the file path in the message.

expert_profile_save_test, CPU only): a version 1 file loads; the same bytes
with the version field at 2 or 0 are refused naming the version and the
file; a version 2 file of another geometry is refused by its version, not
its geometry; back at 1 it loads again.

strata-vision: flash attention off on the CPU only when ggml has AVX-512

ggml's tiled CPU flash-attention kernel needs the head size (72 in this
encoder) to be a multiple of the vector width: 8 floats with AVX2, 16 with
AVX-512. With AVX-512, which a build from source gets on a CPU that has it,
ggml falls back to a kernel that is several times slower and accumulates in
FP16. The release builds are AVX2, where flash attention is the faster one,
so auto stays the default there.

with it, 14.0-15.2 s without; AVX-512 43.5 s with it (26% off the FP32
output), 13.3 s without. --gpu keeps auto, and an explicit --flash-attn
still wins.

docs: the expert cache size is a budget, and an over-sized one pages on Windows

--expert-cache N is N times the largest blob, compared only with the free VRAM
read before the slots are written; the check that runs once they are written is

over-committed allocation goes to system memory instead of failing, so only the

qsa_prompt_attn: Volta m8n8k4 kernel - hi and lo halves in separate accumulator chains

Follow-up to #600 (fks's mma.m8n8k4 prompt attention for sm_70).

The kernel splits q (for q.k) and p (for p.v) into FP16 hi + lo halves
and runs both products into the same accumulator. Volta's tensor cores
don't keep full FP32 precision while they accumulate, so once the hi
products are in the accumulator most of the much smaller lo
contribution gets truncated away, and the split buys less than it
should. Giving the lo products their own chain and adding the two in
FP32 at the end fixes that.

qsa_select: FP32 tiled block scores below sm_80 (opt-in: STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1)

Based on konijiwa110's PR #742. Below sm_80 there is no TF32 tensor-core scorer, so the prompt path scores the QSA
blocks on the warp kernel: 5 shuffles per 4 products, ~1 TFLOPS on an RTX 2080 Ti, 24% of a 128K prompt. With

author's measurement (128K prompt 1,016 to 1,242 tok/s, 248K 715 to 952 on one 2080 Ti).

default below sm_80; here it is opt-in, so default output is unchanged until an interleaved A/B of at least 10 pairs
supports a default. The tail block keeps the warp kernel's arithmetic. STRATA_SELECT_OLD=1 still forces the warp kernel.

HIP: a failed first configure no longer leaves the kernels at -O0

CMake caches CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS_<CONFIG> while it enables HIP, from the
values its platform files set once the compiler is identified. When
HIP cannot compile CMake's identification source, that configure
caches them empty and then stops; every later configure of the same
build folder keeps the cached values, so the build that finally works
compiles every HIP source without -O, i.e. at -O0, while C and C++ get
-O3 -DNDEBUG. setup configures build-hip every time, so one failed
attempt is enough.

That happened on an RX 6800 (Windows 11, HIP SDK 7.2, CMake 4.0.1):
the first attempt failed on Visual Studio 2026's <cmath>, the next one
passed with the include fix, and the engine (0.1.30 with the Windows
build of #247, --expert-cache 2048) decoded at 0.24-0.27 tok/s with
7.1-7.5 s per decode window. STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE put the time in
the GPU's own stages (per window: q8+qkv GEMVs 1468 ms and out-proj
849 ms in the DeltaNet layers, the LM head 540 ms); the waits for flags
the CPU raises were 41 ms of its 8.4 s per window. With the flags back:
59-62 ms per window, 28.1-28.3 tok/s.

After enable_language(HIP), hip_backend.cmake gives each empty
per-configuration HIP flag the value CMake computed for the compiler
(CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS_<CONFIG>_INIT), which is what a fresh build folder
gets. Flags with a value, from CMake or the command line, are left
alone; one set empty on purpose is filled too.

Reproduced on Windows (HIP SDK 7.2, CMake 4.0.1) with a first
configure that failed on --rocm-path flags split at the space in
C:/Program Files, and on Linux (CMake 3.28, TheRock's ROCm 7.10 clang)
with one that failed on a --rocm-device-lib-path that does not exist.
After a working second configure in the same folder,
CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS_RELEASE stays empty and native_mmvq.cu compiles
without -O; with this change it gets -O3 -DNDEBUG. A fresh folder gets
-O3 -DNDEBUG either way.
